scenario: 面试只有 45 分钟，面试官要求先钉死基础范围，范围外的能力一律不建模。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes, and the interviewer wants the base scope pinned down first — anything outside it does not get modeled.
q: BookMyShow 基础需求包含哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: Which capabilities belong in the base BookMyShow design? (select all that apply)
options: 按标题搜索电影
浏览某个影院的未来场次
用户选择具体座位并一次预订多个座位
支付处理和座位差异定价
why: 基础系统覆盖搜索、浏览、查看座位、预订、并发防重和取消。支付、座位类型、价格和改签被排除。
why_en: The base movie-booking design covers search, browsing, seat selection, booking, concurrency, and cancellation, but not payment or pricing.
options_en: Search movies by title.
Browse a theater's upcoming showtimes.
Let a user pick specific seats and book several in one reservation.
Payment processing and per-seat differential pricing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本设计案例中的电影订票系统，用户可搜索电影、选座并预订。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BookMyShow is the movie-ticket booking system this design case is built around, where users search, pick seats, and book.

optionExplanations: 按标题搜索命中的是电影目录本身，是最基础的入口能力，属于范围内。
浏览影院未来场次让用户在下单前看到可选时段，也在基础范围内。
多选座位一次性预订是核心下单动作，必须支持，否则连基本预订都做不到。
支付和差异定价属于产品明确排除的范围，加进来会让基础模型背上不需要的状态。
optionExplanations_en: Title search is the basic movie catalog lookup, so it's in scope.
Browsing a theater's upcoming showtimes lets users see options before booking, also in scope.
Picking multiple seats in one reservation is the core booking action the base design must support.
Payment and per-seat pricing are explicitly excluded from the base design, so adding them pulls in state the scope doesn't need.

q: 补全标准座位布局：
q_en: Fill in the standard seat layout.
text: 每个 screen 使用相同座位布局：行 {{A-Z}}，每行座位号 {{0-20}}，所以每个 showtime 有 {{546}} 个座位。
why: 这是产品给定的规格，不是公式推导出来的：行范围和列范围决定了 546 这个每场座位总数，它是 getAvailableSeats 全量扫描的规模上限。
why_en: This is a given layout spec rather than a derived formula, and the resulting 546-seat count sets the scan size for getAvailableSeats.
scenario: 所有 screen 统一座位布局，前端要用这个规格预渲染整张座位图，并算出每场次的座位总数。
scenario_en: Every screen uses the same seat layout, so the client pre-renders the seating chart and computes the seat count per showtime.

scenario: 面试官同意所有 screen 都采用同一座位布局，只需要告诉用户在哪个厅看。
scenario_en: The interviewer agrees every screen uses the same seat layout, and users only need to know which hall they are in.
q: Screen 应该如何建模？
q_en: How should Screen be modeled?
options: 独立类，拥有 seat map 和 booking logic
Showtime 上的 screenLabel 字符串字段
Reservation 的子类
Movie 上的全局常量
why: Screen 不维护差异化状态，也不执行业务规则，只是“Screen 3”这类导航标签。降级为字段能减少无意义实体。
why_en: Screen can be a label because standardized layouts remove its state and behavior.
whenOtherWins: 如果不同厅有不同座位布局、无障碍座、屏幕属性或维护状态，Screen 才值得成为实体。
options_en: A standalone class with its own seat map and booking logic.
A screenLabel string field on Showtime.
A subclass of Reservation.
A global constant on Movie.
tradeoff: 轻量字符串字段 vs 承载状态和逻辑的独立实体类
optionExplanations: 独立类适合厅与厅座位布局、无障碍座位或屏幕属性不同、需要各自维护状态的场景；本题所有厅同构，用不上这套复杂度。
既然所有 screen 统一布局，Screen 就没有独立状态或行为，用 Showtime.screenLabel 字符串就够标出在哪个厅。
Screen 和 Reservation 是完全不同的概念——一个是放映厅标签，一个是订票记录，做成子类会把两件事绑死。
全局常量意味着所有影院共用同一个值，但每个 showtime 其实在不同的厅，常量表达不出这个归属关系。
optionExplanations_en: A standalone class earns its keep when halls differ in seat layout, accessible seats, or screen attributes and each needs its own state; here every hall is identical, so that overhead buys nothing.
Since every hall shares the same layout, Screen carries no independent state or behavior, so a plain screenLabel string on Showtime is enough to say which hall a showing is in.
Screen and Reservation are unrelated concepts — one labels a hall, the other records a booking — subclassing ties two things that shouldn't be coupled.
A global constant would be shared by every theater, but each showtime actually belongs to a specific hall, so a constant can't express that ownership.

scenario: 用户选择 A5、A6 这类座位；当前系统不需要座位价格、状态机或锁对象。
scenario_en: Users choose seats like A5 and A6; the base system does not need seat prices, state machines, or lock objects.
q: Seat 最适合怎么表示？
q_en: What is the best representation for Seat?
options: 含有价格、锁和 bookedBy 的实体
字符串 ID，例如 A5
Movie 的字段
Theater 的枚举
why: 座位在基础范围内只是稳定标识，不拥有行为。字符串自带相等和哈希，足够作为预订列表元素。
why_en: A seat can be a string identifier when it has no behavior beyond equality and hashing.
whenOtherWins: 如果采用 per-seat locking、座位等级、无障碍属性或独立生命周期，就应把 Seat 升级为类。
options_en: An entity carrying price, a lock, and bookedBy.
A plain string ID, like A5.
A field on Movie.
An enum on Theater.
tradeoff: 轻量字符串标识 vs 携带锁和状态的实体类

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程互斥访问共享状态时使用的同步原语，一次只允许一个线程持有。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock is a synchronization primitive that lets only one thread mutate shared state at a time.

optionExplanations: 一旦要做 per-seat 锁、分级定价或无障碍属性这类每座位独立状态，才值得把 Seat 升级成带锁和字段的实体类。
基础范围内座位没有价格、锁或独立生命周期，字符串自带相等和哈希，足够当预订列表里的一个元素。
座位属于某场放映的某个位置，不是电影的属性，挂在 Movie 上会把两个不相关的维度混在一起。
座位号是每场放映内可选的值，不是 Theater 级别固定不变的取值集合，用枚举既僵化又表达错了归属。
optionExplanations_en: Once you need per-seat locking, tiered pricing, or accessibility attributes — state that differs seat by seat — Seat is worth promoting to a class with a lock.
In the base scope a seat has no price, lock, or lifecycle of its own; a string already gives equality and hashing, which is all a reservation list needs.
A seat belongs to one position in one showing, not to the movie itself, so putting it on Movie mixes two unrelated dimensions.
Seat numbers are a per-showing selection, not a fixed set of values scoped to a Theater, so an enum is both rigid and points at the wrong owner.

scenario: 同一部电影在 3 家影院每天各 8 场，两个用户同一秒抢同一场的 A5 座位。
scenario_en: The same movie runs eight showings a day in three theaters, and two users grab seat A5 of one showing in the same second.
q: 哪个类拥有某一场具体电影的座位状态和预订并发控制？
q_en: Which class owns the seat state and booking concurrency for one movie screening?
options: Movie
Theater
Showtime
BookingSystem
why: 每个 showtime 是真正可预订单位：同一电影在不同时间或影院有不同座位状态。把状态放在 Showtime 可以把并发锁粒度控制在单场。
why_en: Showtime owns booking state because each screening has its own seat availability and concurrency boundary.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class BookingSystem
  class Showtime
  class Reservation
  class Movie
  BookingSystem --> Showtime
  Showtime --> Movie
  Showtime --> Reservation
  Showtime : reservedSeats
  Showtime : bookingLock
options_en: Movie
Theater
Showtime
BookingSystem

termDefinitions.meaning: 协调多个并发操作访问共享状态，避免出现冲突结果的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concurrency control coordinates simultaneous operations on shared state so they don't produce conflicting results.

optionExplanations: Movie 只是电影的元数据，同一部电影在不同场次座位状态完全不同，放在 Movie 上没法区分场次。
Theater 管的是一批 showtime 的容器，把座位状态放这层会让锁覆盖整个影院，粒度太粗。
同一部电影在不同时间或影院各有独立座位状态，Showtime 是这份状态和并发锁自然的归属层。
BookingSystem 是全局编排者，管路由和索引；把座位状态放这里会让每次订票都碰全局锁，粒度太粗。
optionExplanations_en: Movie is just metadata about the film; the same movie has completely different seat state per showing, so Movie can't tell showings apart.
Theater is a container holding many showtimes, so putting seat state there would make one lock cover the whole theater — too coarse.
Each screening of a movie has its own independent seat state, so Showtime is the natural owner of that state and its concurrency lock.
BookingSystem is the global orchestrator for routing and indexes; putting seat state there would make every booking touch a global lock.

scenario: 面试官确认所有厅布局相同、不做座位定价，要求最终实体清单尽量精简。
scenario_en: The interviewer confirms every hall shares one layout and there is no per-seat pricing, and wants the final entity list kept minimal.
q: 最终实体设计中哪些是类？（多选）
q_en: Which objects are classes in the final entity model? (select all that apply)
options: BookingSystem（编排者，管理索引与流程）
Movie（可搜索实体，串联多场放映）
Theater（拥有 showtime 列表的容器）
Showtime（拥有座位状态与并发控制）
Reservation（预订记录，回指 Showtime）
Seat（含 lock 和 bookedBy 的完整实体类）
Screen（拥有座位布局的独立实体类）
why: 这五个对象都有查询、连接或状态职责，被建成类；Seat 在基础范围内是字符串标识，Screen 只是 Showtime 上的字符串字段，都不需要额外的类。
why_en: BookingSystem, Movie, Theater, Showtime, and Reservation are classes because each owns queries, connections, or state, while Seat and Screen stay lightweight strings.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class BookingSystem
  class Movie
  class Theater
  class Showtime
  class Reservation
  BookingSystem --> Showtime
  Showtime --> Movie
  Showtime --> Reservation
options_en: BookingSystem (orchestrator managing indexes and flow).
Movie (searchable entity linking showtimes together).
Theater (container that owns a list of showtimes).
Showtime (owns seat state and concurrency control).
Reservation (booking record that references Showtime back).
Seat (a full entity class with lock and bookedBy).
Screen (a standalone entity class owning a seat layout).
optionExplanations: BookingSystem 承担索引和路由职责，这些是行为而非静态数据，值得做成类。
Movie 要被搜索、被多个 showtime 引用，是有身份、可查询的实体，做成类合理。
Theater 持有一批 showtime 列表并管理归属关系，是有结构的容器实体，值得做类。
Showtime 拥有座位状态和并发锁，是全系统状态最重的对象，必须是类。
Reservation 是不可变的订票记录，要被索引、要能反向路由到 Showtime，做成类合理。
Seat 在基础范围没有价格、锁或独立生命周期，字符串就够表达一个座位标识，不需要额外实体类。
所有厅统一座位布局后，Screen 没有自己的差异化状态可维护，用一个标注所在放映厅的字段代替独立类就够了。
optionExplanations_en: BookingSystem owns indexing and routing behavior, not just static data, so it earns a class.
Movie has identity, gets searched, and is referenced by many showtimes, so it's a proper queryable entity.
Theater holds a list of showtimes and manages that ownership, giving it real structure worth modeling as a class.
Showtime owns seat state and the concurrency lock, the heaviest state in the whole system, so it must be a class.
Reservation is an immutable booking record that gets indexed and routes back to its Showtime, so a class fits.
In the base scope Seat has no price, lock, or lifecycle of its own; a string already carries a seat's identity without a separate class.
Once every hall shares one layout, Screen has no differentiated state left, so it downgrades to a string field on Showtime instead of a class.

scenario: Showtime 需要判断哪些座位已被订，并支持取消后释放座位。
scenario_en: Showtime must know which seats are booked and free them after cancellation.
q: 本文默认选择的单一事实来源是什么？
q_en: What is the default single source of truth in this design?
options: 每个 Seat 对象的 booked flag
BookingSystem 的全局 bookedSeats map
Showtime.reservations 列表
Theater 的 occupiedRows 数组
why: Reservation 本身包含 seatIds，因此所有 reservation 的集合就能推导已订座位。减少第二份 bookedSeats 状态能降低同步错误。
why_en: The reservations list is the source of truth because booked seats are exactly the seats inside active reservations.
whenOtherWins: 如果 availability 检查成为瓶颈，可以维护 bookedSeats Set，但每次 book/cancel 必须和 reservations 同步。
options_en: A booked flag on every Seat object.
A global bookedSeats map on BookingSystem.
The Showtime.reservations list.
An occupiedRows array on Theater.
tradeoff: 单一事实来源（reservations）vs 额外维护的第二份状态

termDefinitions.term: source of truth / 事实来源
termDefinitions.meaning: 系统里被认定为权威、其余状态都从它派生的那份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the authoritative data that every other derived state must agree with.

optionExplanations: 在每个 Seat 上加 booked flag 能做到 O(1) 查询，但会和 reservations 变成两份真相，写路径要两处同步。
全局 bookedSeats map 同样是 O(1)，可当 availability 检查真的成为瓶颈时再引入，否则只是多一份要同步的冗余状态。
reservations 本身就带 seatIds，已订座位能直接从它推导出来，不用额外维护、也就没有同步错误的空间。
occupiedRows 按 theater 粒度算，而座位占用其实按 showtime 区分，粒度先天对不上。
optionExplanations_en: A booked flag on every Seat gives O(1) lookup, but it becomes a second truth alongside reservations, needing two-place sync on every write.
A global bookedSeats map is also O(1) and worth adding once availability checks become an actual bottleneck; otherwise it's one more copy to keep in sync.
Reservations already carry seatIds, so booked seats can be derived directly from them — no extra state to maintain, no room for it to drift.
occupiedRows is scoped per theater, but seat occupancy is really scoped per showtime, so the granularity is wrong from the start.

q: 补全核心关系：
q_en: Fill in the core object relationships.
text: BookingSystem 持有 {{List<Theater>}}；Theater 持有 {{List<Showtime>}}；Showtime 引用 {{Movie}} 并保存 {{List<Reservation>}}；Reservation 反向引用 {{Showtime}}。
why: 反向引用让取消时能从 reservation 找回所属场次，不必全系统扫描。关系清晰比把所有数据塞进 orchestrator 更易维护。
why_en: Reservation keeps a Showtime back-reference so cancellation can route directly to the state owner.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  M["Movie"] --> S["Showtime"]
  T["Theater"] --> S
  S --> R["Reservation"]
  R --> Seats["seat ids"]
  S --> State["reserved seat set"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 子对象反过来持有指向父对象的引用，用于快速回溯归属关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A back-reference lets a child object point back to its owner so code can route directly to it.

scenario: 用户只提供 confirmationId 要取消预订，系统需要释放该预订的座位。
scenario_en: A user provides only a confirmationId to cancel, and the system must release that reservation's seats.
q: Reservation 为什么要保存 showtime 反向引用？
q_en: Why should Reservation keep a Showtime back-reference?
options: 让 Reservation 自己修改所有影院数据
为了搜索电影标题
为了替代 confirmationId
取消时能直接路由到拥有座位状态的 Showtime
why: 取消需要修改 Showtime 的 reservations 列表。反向引用避免从所有 theater/showtime/reservation 中做 O(n) 查找。
why_en: The Showtime back-reference lets cancellation reach the object that owns the seat state.
whenOtherWins: 如果使用数据库或全局 reservationId 索引，也仍可通过外键或索引找到 showtime；核心是取消要路由到状态拥有者。
options_en: It lets Reservation modify all theater data itself.
It exists to search movie titles.
It exists to replace confirmationId.
It lets cancellation route directly to the Showtime that owns the seat state.
tradeoff: back-reference 直接路由 vs 全局扫描查找归属 Showtime

termDefinitions.meaning: 子对象反过来持有指向父对象的引用，用于快速回溯归属关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A back-reference lets a child object point back to its owner so code can route directly to it.

optionExplanations: 反向引用只是让 Reservation 能找到自己的 Showtime，并不是给它权限去改所有影院数据。
搜索电影靠的是 moviesById 和 showtimesByMovieId 索引，跟 Reservation 要不要反向引用没关系。
confirmationId 是外部查找用的主键，back-reference 要解决的是另一件事——从内部找回所属场次。
取消时要从 Showtime 内部改动它保存的预订记录，反向引用能让请求直接路由到状态拥有者，不必逐个扫描所有 theater 和 showtime。
optionExplanations_en: The back-reference just lets Reservation find its own Showtime — it doesn't grant permission to modify all theater data.
Movie search runs through moviesById and showtimesByMovieId indexes; it has nothing to do with whether Reservation holds a back-reference.
confirmationId is the external key used to look up a reservation; the back-reference solves a different problem — routing back to the showing it belongs to.
Cancellation has to mutate the Showtime's reservations list, and the back-reference lets it route straight to that state owner instead of scanning every theater and showtime.

scenario: 用户搜索“Inception”，需要返回可预订的影院和时间，而不只是电影对象。
scenario_en: A user searches for "Inception" and needs bookable theaters and times, not just the movie object.
q: searchMovies(title) 应返回什么更有用？
q_en: What should searchMovies(title) return to be useful?
options: 匹配电影的未来 Showtime 列表
只返回 Movie.title 字符串
所有 Theater 对象不筛选
一个布尔值
why: 用户下一步是选场次和座位，因此返回可行动 showtime 更直接。只返回电影名会导致客户端再做一轮查询。
why_en: Search should return actionable future showtimes rather than just movie titles.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品只是电影目录浏览而非订票入口，返回 Movie 列表会更合适。
options_en: The matching movie's future showtimes.
Just the Movie.title string.
Every Theater object, unfiltered.
A single boolean.
tradeoff: 返回可直接预订的 showtime 列表 vs 只返回电影名逼前端二次查询
optionExplanations: 用户下一步就是选场次和座位，直接返回可预订的未来 showtime 列表能让客户端立刻行动，不用再发一轮查询。
只返回电影名等于没告诉前端能不能订、什么时候订，还得再发一次请求去查场次。
不筛选就返回全部 Theater，等于把过滤工作甩给前端，也会把和这部电影无关的影院混进结果。
布尔值只能回答有没有，回答不了用户接下来要选哪个场次、哪个影院这类可行动的信息。
optionExplanations_en: The user's next step is picking a showtime and seats, so returning the bookable future showtimes directly lets the client act without another round trip.
Returning just the movie title tells the client nothing about whether or when it's bookable, forcing a second request to fetch showtimes.
Returning every Theater unfiltered just pushes filtering onto the client and mixes in theaters that have nothing to do with this movie.
A boolean can only answer yes or no; it can't carry the actionable info the user needs next, like which showtime or theater to pick.

scenario: book 和 cancel 只带 showtimeId 或 confirmationId 进来，对象图里有上百个 theater 和场次。
scenario_en: Booking and cancellation arrive carrying only a showtimeId or a confirmationId, while the object graph holds hundreds of theaters and showings.
q: 为什么 BookingSystem 构造时会建立 showtimesById 和 reservationsById？
q_en: Why does BookingSystem build showtimesById and reservationsById in its constructor?
options: 让所有 Movie 变成可变对象
避免订票和取消时反复扫描所有影院和场次
取代 Showtime 内部用于并发控制的锁机制
强制所有场次按时间排序
why: showtimeId 和 confirmationId 是外部 API 输入，索引能直接路由请求。它们是读路径优化，也表达 lookup 意图。
why_en: Lookup indexes route booking and cancellation requests directly instead of scanning the whole object graph.
options_en: It turns every Movie into a mutable object.
It avoids repeatedly scanning every theater and showtime on booking and cancellation.
It replaces the concurrency-control lock used inside Showtime.
It forces every showtime to sort by time.
tradeoff: 构造期建索引换 O(1) 路由 vs 每次操作都要 O(t×s) 扫描

termDefinitions.meaning: 复杂度记号，t 是 theater 数、s 是每个 theater 的 showtime 数，代表嵌套扫描的规模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(t×s) is complexity notation meaning cost scales with theaters times showtimes per theater, i.e. a nested scan.

optionExplanations: 索引只是加速查找的映射表，跟 Movie 对象是否可变没有任何关系。
showtimeId、confirmationId 都是外部输入的 key，建索引能让订票和取消直接路由，不必每次扫一遍所有 theater 和 showtime。
索引解决的是查找速度，Showtime 内部用来做并发控制的锁解决的是写冲突正确性，两者是不同问题，谁也替代不了谁。
索引按 id 做映射，跟场次要不要按时间排序无关，构建索引不会强加任何排序规则。
optionExplanations_en: Indexes are just lookup maps for speed — they have nothing to do with whether Movie objects are mutable.
showtimeId and confirmationId are external input keys, so indexes let booking and cancellation route directly instead of scanning every theater and showtime each time.
Indexes solve lookup speed; the lock Showtime uses internally for concurrency control solves write-conflict correctness — different problems, and neither substitutes for the other.
Indexes map by id, not by time, so building them imposes no ordering on showtimes at all.

scenario: 构造 BookingSystem 时已拿到全部 theater 和 showtime 数据，但系统还没有任何预订。
scenario_en: When BookingSystem is constructed you already have all theater and showtime data, but the system has no bookings yet.
q: BookingSystem 构造阶段可建立哪些索引？（多选）
q_en: Which indexes can BookingSystem build during construction? (select all that apply)
options: moviesById
showtimesByMovieId
showtimesById
reservationsById 初始为空
why: 前三个从已有 theater/showtime 数据构建，reservationsById 随成功 booking 增长。索引越多，动态更新时越要小心同步。
why_en: The constructor can build movie and showtime indexes, while the reservation index starts empty and grows on bookings.
options_en: moviesById
showtimesByMovieId
showtimesById
reservationsById, which starts empty

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查找而维护的辅助映射结构，通常用 key 直接定位数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is an auxiliary lookup structure maintained purely to speed up finding data by key.

optionExplanations: moviesById 从已有的电影数据直接建出来，让按 id 查电影不用扫描整个列表。
showtimesByMovieId 在构造期从 theater 与 showtime 的关联关系推导出来，让 search 一步到位返回结果。
showtimesById 同样在构造期建好，book 请求靠它直接路由到对应场次。
它在构造时只是一张空表，之后每次成功预订才会写入一条记录，用来给 cancel 做路由。
optionExplanations_en: moviesById is built straight from the existing movie data, so lookups by id skip scanning the whole list.
showtimesByMovieId is derived at construction time from the theater/showtime relationships, so search can return results in one step.
showtimesById is also built at construction time, and booking routes through it straight to the right showing.
reservationsById starts empty at construction and only fills in as bookings succeed, giving cancellation a routing key.

scenario: 用户打开某个影院页面，想知道今天有哪些电影和时间。
scenario_en: A user opens a theater page and wants to see today's movies and showtimes.
q: getShowtimesAtTheater 应返回什么？
q_en: What should getShowtimesAtTheater return?
options: 每部电影单独发一次查询换时间表
包含所有已过期 showtime 一并返回
该影院未来 showtime 列表
只返回影院名称，不含任何场次
why: 一次返回所有未来场次避免先取电影再逐个取时间的 N+1 形状。UI 可以用 showtime.movie 自行分组。
why_en: Returning future showtimes gives the client everything needed to group by movie without N+1 queries.
whenOtherWins: 如果后端直接负责页面聚合，也可以返回按电影分组的 DTO，但领域模型仍可保持 showtime 列表。
options_en: One separate query per movie to fetch its schedule.
All showtimes including already-expired ones.
The theater's future showtimes as one list.
Just the theater name, no showtimes at all.
tradeoff: 一次返回全部 showtime 避免 N+1 vs 逐电影分别查询

termDefinitions.meaning: 先查一次列表，再对列表里每一项各发一次查询，导致请求数随列表长度线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An N+1 query pattern issues one query for a list plus one more query per item, so request count grows with the list size.

optionExplanations: 逐部电影分别查询是典型 N+1 形状，请求数会随电影数线性增长，一次性返回能省掉这一整轮往返。
过去场次已经不能订票，混进结果里只会让用户点了也失败，属于不可操作的数据。
一次性返回该影院全部未来场次，前端能按每条记录自带的电影信息自行分组展示，不用先取电影再逐个查场次。
只给影院名字等于没有任何可预订信息，用户打开页面还是看不到任何场次。
optionExplanations_en: Fetching each movie's schedule separately is a classic N+1 shape — request count grows linearly with the movie count instead of returning everything in one call.
Past showtimes are no longer bookable, so mixing them in just gives the user results that fail when clicked — not actionable data.
Returning the theater's future showtimes in one call lets the client group by showtime.movie itself, skipping the fetch-movie-then-fetch-schedule dance.
Returning only the theater name gives no bookable information at all — the page would still show no showtimes.

scenario: BookingSystem.book 收到 showtimeId 和 seatIds，需要创建预订并委托状态拥有者。
scenario_en: BookingSystem.book receives showtimeId and seatIds, then creates a reservation and delegates to the state owner.
q: 这段伪代码体现了哪种职责分配？
q_en: What responsibility split does this pseudocode show?
codeSample:
book(showtimeId, seatIds)
    showtime = showtimesById[showtimeId]
    reservation = Reservation(generateId(), showtime, seatIds)
    showtime.book(reservation)
    reservationsById[reservation.id] = reservation
    return reservation
options: BookingSystem 完全跳过 Showtime，直接修改座位状态变量
Reservation 自己调用取消并释放座位
Theater 统一持有所有 showtime 的锁
BookingSystem 编排和索引，Showtime 原子校验并保存
why: BookingSystem 只负责路由和创建记录；真正的可用性检查和写入在 Showtime 内完成。失败时 reservation 不会注册到全局索引。
why_en: BookingSystem orchestrates while Showtime performs atomic validation and storage.
whenOtherWins: 如果使用持久化数据库，showtime.book 的原子性可能由事务或唯一约束承载。
options_en: BookingSystem skips Showtime entirely and mutates the seat-state variable directly.
Reservation calls its own cancel and frees the seats itself.
Theater holds a single lock for every showtime under it.
BookingSystem orchestrates and indexes; Showtime does the atomic check-and-store.
tradeoff: 编排者路由与索引 vs 状态拥有者做原子校验和写入

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调其他对象、驱动主流程但不直接持有核心状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An orchestrator coordinates other objects and drives the main flow without owning the core state itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组操作要么全部生效要么完全不生效，中途不会被其他线程看到中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Atomic means a set of operations either all take effect or none do, with no other thread observing a half-done state.

optionExplanations: 伪代码里编排层调用的是 showtime.book(reservation)，座位状态的改动仍然发生在 Showtime 内部，并没有被跳过。
这段代码是 book 流程，压根没有出现取消逻辑，Reservation 也没有主动调用任何方法。
锁写在 Showtime 内部（体现在后续 synchronized 用法），不是 Theater 层面的统一锁，粒度被这段代码框定在单场。
这正是图里体现的分工：路由和建索引留在编排层，真正判断能不能订、要不要落地交给状态拥有者处理。
optionExplanations_en: The pseudocode has BookingSystem call showtime.book(reservation) — the seat-state change still happens inside Showtime, it isn't skipped.
This snippet is the booking flow; cancellation logic never appears here, and Reservation doesn't call anything on its own.
The lock lives inside Showtime (as later synchronized usage shows), not at the Theater level — this code scopes it to one showing.
BookingSystem just routes to the right showtime and writes the index; the actual availability check and storage happen inside showtime.book, so a failure never pollutes the index.

scenario: 用户同时选择 A5、A6、A7，但 A6 已被别人预订。
scenario_en: A user selects A5, A6, and A7, but A6 has already been booked by someone else.
q: 正确行为是什么？
q_en: What is the correct behavior?
options: 整个预订失败，A5 和 A7 也不能被部分占用
先订 A5 和 A7，跳过 A6
为 A6 生成候补票
把 A6 从别人的 reservation 移过来
why: 多座位预订必须 all-or-nothing。先验证所有座位，再做任何状态修改，才能避免部分成功。
why_en: Multi-seat booking must be all-or-nothing, with all seats validated before storing the reservation.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品支持拆单或推荐替代座位，应显式设计新的用户确认流程，而不是静默部分成功。
options_en: The whole booking fails; A5 and A7 stay unclaimed too.
Book A5 and A7 first and just skip A6.
Generate a waitlist ticket for A6.
Move A6 out of the other user's reservation.
tradeoff: all-or-nothing 原子校验 vs 允许部分成功的静默拆单

termDefinitions.meaning: 多项操作要么全部成功要么全部不生效，不留下部分完成的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: All-or-nothing means a multi-step operation either fully succeeds or leaves no partial state behind.

optionExplanations: 多座位预订必须先校验完全部座位再落地任何状态，一个座位不可用就让整单失败，避免部分成功。
部分成功看似体贴，但会让用户以为订到了三个座位却少一个，还得再处理退款和重新选座。
候补票是产品明确没提过的新功能，基础设计不该在这里临时发明一套排队机制。
把座位从别人的预订里抢走会破坏另一个用户已经成立的预订，直接违反不变量。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-seat booking must validate every seat before committing any state, so one unavailable seat should fail the whole request instead of partially succeeding.
Partial success sounds considerate, but it leaves the user thinking they got all three seats when they didn't, forcing a refund-and-reselect flow afterward.
A waitlist ticket is a feature nobody asked for here — the base design shouldn't invent a queueing mechanism on the spot.
Ripping a seat out of someone else's reservation breaks a booking that already succeeded, a direct violation of the seat-uniqueness invariant.

q: 按正确顺序排列双订座位的竞态链路：
q_en: Put the double-booking race condition in the correct order.
steps: 线程 A 和线程 B 都看到 A5 可用。
两个线程都把包含 A5 的 reservation 加入列表。
check availability 和 add reservation 没有在同一个临界区。
结果两个用户拿到同一座位。
why: 这是典型 check-then-act 竞态。修复方式是把“检查所有座位”和“保存 reservation”放进同一个 Showtime 锁内。
why_en: The double-booking bug is a check-then-act race between availability checking and reservation storage.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U1
  participant S as Showtime
  participant U2
  U1->>S: check A5 free
  U2->>S: check A5 free
  U1->>S: reserve A5
  U2->>S: reserve A5

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检查条件再执行动作，中间没有加锁保护，可能被其他线程插入导致竞态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Check-then-act means checking a condition and then acting on it without holding a lock across both steps, letting another thread interleave and cause a race.

termDefinitions.meaning: 必须互斥执行的代码区间，一次只能有一个线程进入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A critical section is a code region that only one thread may execute at a time.

scenario: 两个用户可能同时预订同一场电影的同一座位。
scenario_en: Two users may book the same seat for the same movie showtime at the same time.
q: 这段 Showtime.book 伪代码的关键保证是什么？
q_en: What guarantee does this Showtime.book pseudocode provide?
codeSample:
book(reservation)
    synchronized(this)
        for seatId in reservation.seatIds
            if !isValidSeatId(seatId) throw InvalidSeat
        for seatId in reservation.seatIds
            if !isAvailable(seatId) throw Unavailable
        reservations.add(reservation)
options: 所有场次共用同一把全局锁串行化
check 和 store 是原子的
座位 ID 永远不需要做合法性验证
取消操作不需要拿任何锁
why: 锁的粒度是单个 Showtime，避免同一场次内双订。不同 showtime 可以并行预订，不受这个锁影响。
why_en: The synchronized block makes the check-and-store sequence atomic for one showtime.
whenOtherWins: 如果单场超高并发成为瓶颈，可以升级为 per-seat locking，但需要排序加锁避免死锁。
options_en: Every showtime shares one single global lock.
The check and the store are atomic together.
Seat IDs never need validity checking.
Cancellation never needs to hold a lock.
tradeoff: check-and-store 在同一临界区 vs 检查和写入分离产生竞态窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段代码用锁包裹，保证同一时刻只有一个线程执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A synchronized block wraps code with a lock so only one thread executes it at a time.

optionExplanations: synchronized(this) 锁的是这一个 Showtime 实例，不同场次各自有各自的锁，并不是全局共用一把。
两次 for 循环（校验合法性、校验可用性）和最后的 add 都包在同一个 synchronized 块里，检查和保存不会被别的线程插进来。
代码第一段 for 循环就是在做 isValidSeatId 校验，合法性检查明明白白写在里面。
这段代码没有对取消做出说明，但 cancel 要和 book 读写同一份 reservations 列表，同样需要拿锁才安全。
optionExplanations_en: synchronized(this) locks this one Showtime instance; every showtime has its own lock, not one shared global lock.
Both validation loops and the final add() sit inside the same synchronized block, so the check and the store can't be interleaved by another thread.
The first for-loop in the snippet is exactly the seatId validity check — it's right there in the code.
This snippet says nothing about cancellation, but cancel reads and writes the same reservations list as book, so it needs the same lock to stay safe.

scenario: 单场 546 座，临界区只是几十个座位的校验加写入，面试要求几十行内写出并发正确的 book。
scenario_en: One showing has 546 seats, the critical section is just validating and writing a few seats, and the interviewer wants a correct book() in a few dozen lines.
q: per-showtime 锁相比 per-seat 锁的主要优点是什么？
q_en: What is the main benefit of per-showtime locking over per-seat locking?
options: 允许同一座位同时被多个用户预订成功
在任何并发场景下吞吐量都必然最高
实现简单、无死锁风险、Seat 保持字符串
座位 ID 是否存在、是否合法的校验都可以省略不做
why: per-showtime 锁把同一场次所有预订串行化，牺牲一些并行度换清晰正确性。基础面试范围内临界区短，通常足够。
why_en: Per-showtime locking is simple and avoids multi-lock deadlock while keeping Seat as a string.
options_en: Lets the same seat be booked by multiple users at once.
Guarantees the highest throughput in any concurrency scenario.
Simple to implement, no multi-lock deadlock risk, Seat stays a string.
Whether a seat ID even exists or is valid can be skipped entirely.
tradeoff: 单锁实现简单 vs 多锁高吞吐但要处理死锁

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个线程互相等待对方持有的锁，谁都无法继续执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock happens when threads each wait for a lock the other is holding, so none can proceed.

optionExplanations: 无论哪种锁粒度，正确实现都必须保证同一座位不能被两个人同时订到，这不是任何一种锁的优点。
这个说法把方向说反了：真正为吞吐量优化的是更细粒度的 per-seat 方案，粗粒度的这种锁恰恰是牺牲并行度换正确性的那一侧。
只用一把锁，不涉及多锁排序，天然没有死锁风险，Seat 也不用升级成带锁的类，是四个选项里实现最简单的一个。
座位是否存在、是否在 A-Z/0-20 范围内，跟用哪种锁粒度无关，两种方案都要做这个校验。
optionExplanations_en: Whatever the lock granularity, a correct implementation must still stop two users from booking the same seat — that's never an advantage of any locking scheme.
Per-showtime locking is exactly what trades away throughput under heavy concurrency — same-showtime bookings queue up; per-seat is the design aimed at higher throughput.
Per-showtime uses a single lock with no multi-lock ordering to worry about, so it has no deadlock risk and Seat can stay a plain string — the simplest implementation.
Whether a seatId is within A-Z/0-20 has nothing to do with lock granularity — both approaches still need that validation.

scenario: 热门首映场同一 showtime 每秒上百人抢不同座位，per-showtime 锁成为瓶颈。
scenario_en: For a hot premiere, hundreds of users per second book different seats in the same showtime, and the per-showtime lock bottlenecks.
q: 更高吞吐的替代设计是什么？
q_en: What alternative design gives higher throughput?
options: 给所有入场请求加上随机延迟来分散压力
直接把 reservationsById 整个索引清空，用来减少扫描开销
把锁的粒度提升到整个 Theater 级别
把 Seat 升级为带锁的类，按 seatId 排序加锁
why: per-seat locking 只阻塞争抢相同座位的预订。多座位预订必须按稳定顺序加锁，否则可能死锁。
why_en: Per-seat locking improves throughput but requires sorted lock acquisition to avoid deadlock.
whenOtherWins: 普通场次或面试基础范围用 per-showtime 锁更稳，除非明确需要优化同场并发。
options_en: Add random delay to every incoming request to spread out load.
Delete the entire reservationsById index outright to cut scanning overhead.
Raise the lock's granularity all the way up to the whole Theater.
Promote Seat to a class with a lock, acquiring locks in sorted seatId order.
tradeoff: per-seat 锁提高吞吐 vs 排序加锁与双份状态的复杂度代价

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个座位单独一把锁，只有争抢同一座位的请求才会互相阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-seat locking gives every seat its own lock, so only requests contending for the same seat block each other.

optionExplanations: 随机延迟只是让请求变慢，并不会让互相独立的座位预订真正并行起来，吞吐量并没有提升。
reservationsById 是 reservation 的事实来源索引，清空它会让可用性和取消都失效，这是破坏正确性，不是优化。
把锁提升到 Theater 级别是往粗粒度反方向走，会让同一影院所有场次的预订都排队，吞吐量只会更差。
把 Seat 升级成带锁的类，只阻塞真正争抢同一座位的请求，不同座位可以并行；多锁场景下按 seatId 排序获取能避免死锁。
optionExplanations_en: Random delay just slows requests down; it doesn't make independent seat bookings run in parallel, so throughput doesn't actually improve.
reservationsById is the source-of-truth index for reservations — clearing it breaks availability and cancellation, which is a correctness bug, not an optimization.
Raising the lock to the Theater level moves toward coarser granularity, serializing every showtime's bookings in that theater — throughput gets worse, not better.
Promoting Seat to a lockable class only blocks requests contending for the same seat, letting different seats book in parallel; acquiring locks in sorted seatId order avoids deadlock.

q: 补全 per-seat locking 的死锁规避规则：
q_en: Fill in the deadlock-avoidance rule for per-seat locking.
text: 多座位预订要先对 seatIds 做{{排序}}，所有线程都按同一顺序获取锁，避免 A 锁 A5 等 A6、B 锁 A6 等 A5 的{{循环等待}}。
why: 一旦一次操作需要拿多把锁，稳定加锁顺序就是最基本的死锁预防。这个复杂度是 per-seat 方案的主要代价。
why_en: Sorted lock acquisition prevents circular waits when a booking needs multiple seat locks.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["selected seats"] --> B["sort seat ids"]
  B --> C["lock A5"]
  C --> D["lock A6"]
  D --> E["check and reserve"]
  E --> F["release reverse order"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个线程互相持有对方需要的锁，形成等待环，谁都无法前进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circular wait is when each thread holds a lock another thread needs, forming a cycle where nobody can proceed.

scenario: 座位状态只存在 Showtime 里，前端要渲染座位图，用户一次提交多个座位的预订。
scenario_en: Seat state lives only inside Showtime, the client renders a seat map, and a user submits several seats in one booking.
q: Showtime 的核心方法通常包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core methods does Showtime usually expose? (select all that apply)
options: isAvailable(seatId)
getAvailableSeats()
book(reservation)
cancel(reservation)
why: 这四个方法都围绕单场次座位状态展开。查询和修改都集中在 Showtime，有助于维持不变量。
why_en: Showtime centers the seat-state operations: availability, listing, booking, and cancellation.
options_en: isAvailable(seatId) — checks one seat.
getAvailableSeats() — lists every open seat.
book(reservation) — validates and stores a booking.
cancel(reservation) — removes a booking and frees seats.
optionExplanations: isAvailable(seatId) 只查单个座位是否空着，是最小粒度的可用性检查。
getAvailableSeats() 把整场的可选座位一次性列出来，前端渲染座位图要用到它。
book(reservation) 是写路径的入口，在锁内完成校验和保存。
cancel(reservation) 负责把座位从 reservations 里移除，释放给别人预订。
optionExplanations_en: isAvailable(seatId) checks a single seat's status — the finest-grained availability query.
getAvailableSeats() lists every open seat in the showing at once, which the client needs to render the seat map.
book(reservation) is the write-path entry point, doing validation and storage inside the lock.
cancel(reservation) removes a seat from reservations, freeing it up for someone else to book.

scenario: 前端座位图需要知道哪些座位可选，基础布局固定。
scenario_en: The client seat map needs to know which seats are selectable, and the base layout is fixed.
q: getAvailableSeats 的合理做法是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable getAvailableSeats implementation?
options: 按 reservations 推导已订座位再过滤布局
返回全部座位，完全不检查任何 reservation
只返回第一排 A 排的座位列表
调用支付系统的状态来判断座位是否可用
why: reservations 是事实来源，booked set 是局部派生结构。固定布局扫描成本是常数级，足够清晰。
why_en: Available seats can be derived by subtracting booked seats from the fixed layout.
whenOtherWins: 如果布局可变，应让 Screen 或 SeatLayout 提供完整座位集合，而不是硬编码 A-Z/0-20。
options_en: Derive booked seats from reservations, then filter the layout.
Return every seat without checking any reservation at all.
Return only the seats in row A.
Ask the payment system's state to decide seat availability.
tradeoff: 从 reservations 派生可用座位 vs 维护第二份 bookedSeats 状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 不单独存储，而是每次从权威数据现算出来的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Derived state is not stored on its own; it is computed on demand from the authoritative data.

optionExplanations: 既然事实来源是 reservations，先从里面统计出已订座位集合，再拿固定布局减去它，逻辑清晰也不引入新状态。
不检查任何 reservation 就等于把已经订出去的座位也当成可选，会直接导致双订。
座位图有 A-Z 整个范围，只返回 A 排既不完整也没有任何设计理由。
支付流程在这道题的基础范围之外，座位是否可用只取决于有没有 active reservation，跟支付系统状态无关。
optionExplanations_en: Since reservations are the source of truth, collecting a booked set from them and subtracting it from the fixed layout gives available seats cleanly, with no new state to introduce.
Skipping the reservation check entirely means already-booked seats would still show as selectable, a direct path to double-booking.
The layout spans rows A through Z; returning only row A is both incomplete and unmotivated by anything in the design.
Payment is out of scope for this base design, and seat availability depends only on active reservations, not on any payment system state.

scenario: 用户提交 seatId='AA99' 或 'Z21'。
scenario_en: The user submits seatId='AA99' or 'Z21'.
q: Showtime.book 应如何处理？
q_en: How should Showtime.book handle it?
options: 先保存 reservation，出问题再异步清理
在锁内校验 seatId 属于 A-Z/0-20
把不合法的座位当成已售罄处理
把校验逻辑交给 Movie 类来做
why: 座位合法性和可用性都要在同一原子 booking 流程里检查。无效输入不能创建 reservation。
why_en: Seat IDs should be validated inside the atomic booking flow before any reservation is stored.
whenOtherWins: 如果座位布局由外部配置提供，校验应委托给 SeatLayout，但仍要在写入前完成。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["book(seats)"] --> L["showtime lock"]
  L --> B{"all seats free?"}
  B -- no --> R["reject"]
  B -- yes --> C["mark seats reserved"]
  C --> D["create reservation"]
options_en: Store the reservation first and clean up asynchronously later.
Validate every seatId is within A-Z / 0-20 inside the lock.
Treat an invalid seat as already sold out.
Delegate seat validation to the Movie class.
tradeoff: 写入前原子校验合法性 vs 先写后清理留下脏状态窗口
codeSample:
isValidSeatId(seatId)
    row = seatId[0]
    num = parseInt(seatId.substring(1))
    return row >= 'A' && row <= 'Z'
        && num >= 0 && num <= 20
optionExplanations: 先写入再异步清理会有一段时间窗口，让一个根本不存在的座位出现在 reservations 里，破坏了 all-or-nothing。
座位合法性和可用性都属于写入前必须完成的校验，放进同一个锁内能保证无效输入不会创建出任何 reservation。
把非法座位当成售罄会让错误信息失真——用户会以为座位存在只是被订走了，而不是输入本身就错了。
座位号的格式规则跟电影毫无关系，Movie 类完全不知道座位布局，交给它做校验找错了对象。
optionExplanations_en: Storing the reservation first and cleaning up asynchronously leaves a window where a seat that never existed sits in reservations, breaking all-or-nothing.
Seat validity and availability both need to pass before anything is written, and checking them inside the same lock guarantees invalid input never creates a reservation.
Treating an invalid seat as sold out gives a misleading error — the user would think the seat exists and was taken, not that their input was wrong.
Seat-id format rules have nothing to do with movies; Movie doesn't even know the seating layout, so it's the wrong place to validate them.

scenario: 用户取消 confirmationId，系统已经通过 reservationsById 找到 reservation。
scenario_en: A user cancels by confirmationId, and the system has found the reservation through reservationsById.
q: 这段取消流程为什么能释放座位？
q_en: Why does this cancellation flow free the seats?
codeSample:
cancelReservation(id)
    reservation = reservationsById[id]
    showtime = reservation.getShowtime()
    showtime.cancel(reservation)
    reservationsById.remove(id)

Showtime.cancel(reservation)
    synchronized(this)
        reservations.remove(reservation)
options: 必须对每个座位调用 Seat.markFree 才能真正释放
取消操作只删除全局索引，座位状态完全不受影响
座位可用性由 reservations 推导，删除即释放
取消这件事应该交给 Movie 类来完成
why: 因为没有第二份 bookedSeats 状态，取消只需从 Showtime 的 reservations 中删除。全局索引也要删除，防止重复取消。
why_en: Removing the reservation from Showtime frees its seats because availability is derived from the reservation list.
whenOtherWins: 如果维护 bookedSeats Set，取消必须同时从 reservations 和 bookedSeats 中删除。
options_en: Every seat needs its own Seat.markFree call to actually free it.
Cancellation only deletes the global index and leaves seat state untouched.
Availability is derived from reservations, so removing one frees its seats.
Cancellation should be handled by the Movie class.
tradeoff: 删除即释放的派生状态 vs 需要额外一步同步第二份座位状态

termDefinitions.term: source of truth / 事实来源
termDefinitions.meaning: 系统里被认定为权威、其余状态都从它派生的那份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the authoritative data that every other derived state must agree with.

optionExplanations: Seat 在基础设计里只是字符串，没有 markFree 这样的方法可调用，座位状态本来就不是它自己维护的。
代码里 showtime.cancel 明明从 reservations 里移除了这条记录，座位状态确实跟着变了，不是只删了索引。
可用性本来就是从 reservations 现算出来的派生状态，把这条 reservation 从列表删掉，它占的座位自然就不再计入已订。
取消动作要改的是 Showtime 内部保存的预订记录，跟 Movie 完全没有关系，不该由它来处理。
optionExplanations_en: In the base design Seat is just a string with no markFree method to call — seat state was never something Seat maintained on its own.
The code's showtime.cancel actually removes the entry from reservations, so seat state does change — it's not just deleting an index.
Availability is derived on the fly from reservations, so removing this reservation from the list automatically stops counting its seats as booked.
Cancellation mutates Showtime's reservations list; Movie has no relationship to seat state at all, so it's the wrong owner for this.

rows: 删 key 防重复取消

scenario: 目录里同时有 1984 版和 2021 版《Dune》，每个 showtime 必须指向正确的那一部。
scenario_en: The catalog carries both the 1984 and the 2021 Dune, and every showtime has to point at the right one.
q: Movie 为什么要有 id 而不只存 title？
q_en: Why does Movie need an id instead of only a title?
options: 给 title 字段加唯一索引就能防止两部电影重名
id 用来表示座位号
Movie 不该被引用
重映或翻拍可能同名，id 才是稳定身份
why: 用户按标题搜索，但系统内部需要稳定唯一身份连接 showtime。两个 Dune 或同名电影不应被混为一谈。
why_en: Movie needs an ID because titles are searchable but not guaranteed unique.
options_en: Adding a unique index on title would stop two movies from sharing a name.
The ID represents a specific seat number.
Movie objects should never be referenced by anything.
A remake or re-release can share a title, so the ID is the stable identity.
tradeoff: id 作稳定内部身份 vs title 作用户可搜索但不唯一的标签
optionExplanations: 给 title 加唯一索引确实能挡住完全同名的重复记录，但重映或翻拍电影本就该被允许共享同一个 title，唯一索引反而会拒绝合法数据，替代不了稳定的 id。
座位号是 Seat 的标识（例如 A5），跟 Movie 的 id 是两个完全不相关的字段。
Showtime 恰恰需要引用 Movie 才能知道自己在放哪部电影，Movie 必须能被引用。
重映或翻拍可能和原作同名，title 不保证唯一，只有 id 才能稳定地把 showtime 绑在正确的那部电影上。
optionExplanations_en: A unique index on title would indeed block exact-duplicate rows, but a remake or re-release is legitimately allowed to share its title with the original — the index would reject valid data instead of substituting for a stable id.
A seat number is Seat's identifier (like A5) — that's an entirely different field from Movie's id.
Showtime specifically needs to reference Movie to know which film it's showing, so Movie must be referenceable.
A re-release or remake can share a title with the original, so title isn't guaranteed unique — only the id can stably tie a showtime to the right film.

scenario: Reservation 构造时收到 seatIds 列表，调用方之后可能修改原列表。
scenario_en: Reservation receives a seatIds list in the constructor, and the caller may later mutate that list.
q: Reservation 应该怎么保护自身状态？
q_en: How should Reservation protect its own state?
options: 构造和取值都做 defensive copy
直接保存外部传入的列表引用，不做任何拷贝
让调用方自己保证不会修改这份列表
把 seatIds 存成用逗号拼接的字符串
why: Reservation 是预订记录，创建后不应被外部列表修改。防御性拷贝能保护不可变语义。
why_en: Defensive copies keep a reservation's seat list immutable from external mutation.
whenOtherWins: 在不可变集合默认的语言中，可以直接存不可变列表。
options_en: Defensive-copy both on construction and on read.
Store a direct reference to the caller's list with no copying at all.
Trust the caller to promise it won't mutate the list.
Store seatIds as a comma-joined string.
tradeoff: 构造时防御性拷贝 vs 直接持有外部引用带来的隐式修改风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 构造或返回集合时复制一份，避免外部引用修改内部状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A defensive copy duplicates a collection on the way in or out so external code can't mutate internal state.

optionExplanations: 构造时拷贝一份、getSeatIds 也返回拷贝，外部无论怎么改原始列表或返回值，都碰不到 Reservation 内部真正持有的数据。
直接存引用意味着调用方事后改这个列表，Reservation 内部的座位记录也会跟着被改，破坏了记录应有的不可变性。
口头约定调用方不改，没有任何机制保证，一旦有人忘了或者代码变了，Bug 会悄悄发生。
拼成字符串既丢失了类型信息，还要重新解析才能用，多绕一层却没换来任何保护。
optionExplanations_en: Copying on construction and copying again in getSeatIds means no outside code can touch the list Reservation actually holds internally, no matter how the original or returned list gets mutated.
Holding a direct reference means the caller mutating that list later mutates the reservation's internal seat record too, breaking the immutability a record should have.
Trusting the caller not to mutate it is just a verbal agreement with no enforcement — one forgotten case and the bug happens silently.
Joining into a comma-separated string loses type information and needs re-parsing to use, adding a layer of indirection without buying any real protection.

scenario: book 接口直接暴露给不可信客户端，任何一次失败都不能留下半条 reservation 或索引。
scenario_en: The book endpoint is exposed to untrusted clients, and no failure may leave a half-written reservation or index entry behind.
q: BookingSystem.book 应处理哪些失败情况？（多选）
q_en: Which failure cases should BookingSystem.book handle? (select all that apply)
options: showtimeId 为空或不存在
seatIds 为空
任一 seatId 无效
任一座位已不可用
why: 路由输入、座位合法性和可用性都可能失败。任何失败都不应留下 reservation 或索引记录。
why_en: Booking failures must leave no reservation behind, whether the issue is routing, input, invalid seats, or unavailable seats.
options_en: showtimeId is null or does not exist.
seatIds is empty.
Any seatId is invalid.
Any seat is already unavailable.
optionExplanations: showtimeId 是找 Showtime 的路由 key，为空或查不到就该在最早一步拒绝，不该往下走。
seatIds 为空意味着这单什么都没选，不该生成一条空座位的 reservation。
座位号格式不对（不在 A-Z/0-20 内）说明输入本身有问题，必须在写入前挡住。
座位已经被别人订走同样要拒绝，否则就是最基本的双订。
optionExplanations_en: showtimeId is the routing key to find a Showtime — null or missing should be rejected at the very first step, not carried forward.
An empty seatIds means the request selected nothing, so it shouldn't produce a reservation with zero seats.
A malformed seat id (outside A-Z/0-20) signals bad input and has to be blocked before anything gets written.
A seat someone else already booked must also be rejected — letting it through is a straightforward double-booking.

scenario: 用户搜索电影时，系统里还保留了昨天的 showtime 对象。
scenario_en: A user searches for a movie while yesterday's showtime objects still exist in memory.
q: searchMovies 和 getShowtimesAtTheater 应如何处理？
q_en: How should searchMovies and getShowtimesAtTheater handle them?
options: 把所有过去和未来场次都返回，交给前端自己过滤掉
只返回 future showtimes
直接把 Movie 对象删除掉
把过去的场次当成免费票发放
why: 过去场次不可预订，返回它们会给用户不可操作结果。内存中是否保留旧场次是另一个清理问题。
why_en: Search and browsing should return future showtimes because past showtimes are not bookable.
whenOtherWins: 如果是历史订单或排片管理后台，过去场次才可能需要返回。
options_en: Return every past and future showtime and let the frontend filter them out.
Return only future showtimes.
Delete the Movie object outright.
Treat past showtimes as free tickets to hand out.
tradeoff: 只暴露可操作的未来场次 vs 把不可预订的历史场次也返回给用户

termDefinitions.meaning: 开场时间晚于当前时间、仍可预订的放映场次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A future showtime is a screening whose start time is still ahead of now and therefore still bookable.

optionExplanations: 把过滤逻辑丢给前端，后端还是把不可预订的过去场次混进响应里，用户依旧可能点开一个已经放映完的场次。
只返回还没开场的 showtime，用户看到的每一项都真的能订，不会点进去才发现已经过期。
过去场次是否清理是内存管理问题，跟要不要删掉整个 Movie 对象没有关系——Movie 还要给未来场次用。
免费票是完全没出现过的产品需求，基础设计不该凭空发明一套赠票逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Pushing the filtering to the frontend still means the backend response mixes in unbookable past showtimes, so the user can still tap into one that's already over.
Returning only showtimes that haven't started yet means every item the user sees is actually bookable, with no surprise dead ends.
Whether to clean up past showtimes in memory is a separate housekeeping question — it has nothing to do with deleting the Movie object, which future showtimes still need.
Free tickets are a product requirement that never came up here — the base design shouldn't invent a giveaway mechanism out of nowhere.

q: 成功预订 A5/A6 的正确顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order for successfully booking A5 and A6?
steps: Showtime 在锁内校验 A5/A6 合法且可用。
BookingSystem 通过 showtimesById 找到对应 Showtime。
Showtime 把 reservation 加入自己的 reservations。
BookingSystem 把 confirmationId -> reservation 写入 reservationsById。
why: 状态写入顺序确保 Showtime 先接受预订，全局取消索引后注册。若 Showtime 抛错，索引不会污染。
why_en: The booking flow routes first, atomically stores in Showtime, then registers the confirmation index.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant B as BookingSystem
  participant S as Showtime
  participant R as Reservation
  U->>B: book A5,A6
  B->>S: book seats
  S->>S: check and reserve
  S->>R: create reservation
  S-->>B: reservation id

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 id 直接定位对象的映射表，避免逐个遍历查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A routing index maps an ID straight to its object, avoiding a linear search.

scenario: 后续要求运行时添加新的 showtime，而不是只在构造时加载。
scenario_en: A later requirement allows adding new showtimes at runtime instead of only loading them in the constructor.
q: addShowtime 必须同步更新哪些结构？
q_en: Which structures must addShowtime update in sync?
options: 只把 Theater 的名字字段改一下就完事
只需要把新记录写进 reservationsById 索引里
Theater.showtimes 和三张 By 索引都要更新
什么索引都不需要碰，下次查询会自动全部重建
why: 构造时建立过的所有派生索引，在动态写入时都要同步维护。否则搜索或订票会漏掉新场次。
why_en: Dynamic additions must update every index that the constructor would have populated.
whenOtherWins: 如果索引改为查询时实时扫描，则动态更新更简单但读路径更慢。
options_en: Just tweak the Theater's name field and call it done.
Only write the new record into reservationsById.
Theater.showtimes plus all three By-indexes need updating.
Touch no index at all; the next query rebuilds everything.
tradeoff: 同步更新全部派生索引 vs 只更新部分导致搜索/订票漏掉新场次

termDefinitions.term: denormalized index / 反规范化索引
termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查询而额外维护的冗余结构，写入时必须和主数据保持同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A denormalized index is a redundant lookup structure kept only for speed, and every write must keep it in sync with the source data.

optionExplanations: 新增场次跟 Theater 的名字毫无关系，这个动作根本没有触碰到任何该更新的结构。
reservationsById 是给已成立的预订用的索引，新场次此时还没有任何 reservation，写进这里完全找错了地方。
构造时建立过的所有索引（moviesById、showtimesByMovieId、showtimesById）加上 Theater.showtimes 本身，动态新增时都要同步更新，漏一个就会漏掉这场。
这些索引不是查询时懒计算出来的，是显式维护的结构，不主动写入就永远不会自动出现。
optionExplanations_en: Adding a showtime has nothing to do with the Theater's name field — this action doesn't touch any structure that actually needs updating.
reservationsById is for confirmed bookings; a brand-new showtime has no reservations yet, so writing there is simply the wrong place.

Every index the constructor built (moviesById, showtimesByMovieId, showtimesById) plus Theater.showtimes itself must stay in sync on a dynamic add, or search or booking will silently miss the new showing.
These indexes aren't lazily recomputed on read — they're explicitly maintained structures, so skipping the write means they never catch up on their own.

scenario: 运营要删除某个 showtime，但已有 active reservations。
scenario_en: Operations wants to delete a showtime that already has active reservations.
q: 最安全的基础处理是什么？
q_en: What is the safest base-design behavior?
options: 直接删除 showtime 对象，无主 reservation 留在原地不管
只从 movie index 删除
把票自动挪到任意其他场次
拒绝删除，先取消并通知所有 reservation
why: 删除有票场次会让 confirmationId 和 reservation 指向悬空对象。基础设计应拒绝，等取消和通知完成后再删。
why_en: Removing a showtime with active reservations should be rejected until reservations are handled.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务支持场次取消流程，可发事件给通知监听器并批量退款/取消后再清理索引。
options_en: Delete the showtime object outright and leave orphaned reservations in place.
Only remove it from the movie index.
Automatically move the tickets to some other showtime.
Reject the deletion; cancel and notify every reservation first.
tradeoff: 拒绝删除保护引用完整性 vs 直接删除留下悬空 reservation

termDefinitions.meaning: 指向已经被删除对象的引用，访问它会得到无效或空结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dangling reference points at an object that no longer exists, so following it yields nothing valid.

optionExplanations: 直接删掉 showtime 对象，会让已经发出去的确认码从此找不到对应场次，留在原地的 reservation 变成悬空引用，取消或查询都会出错。
只从 movie index 里摘掉，Theater.showtimes 和 showtimesById 还留着这场的记录，索引之间会互相矛盾。
换一个场次意味着座位号、开场时间全都不一样，自动挪票等于替用户做了一个他没同意的决定。
有 active reservation 时先拒绝删除，等取消和通知都完成、没有悬空引用了，才真正移除这场。
optionExplanations_en: Deleting the showtime object outright leaves existing confirmationIds pointing at a showing that no longer exists — the orphaned reservations become a dangling reference that breaks cancellation and lookups.
Removing it only from the movie index leaves Theater.showtimes and showtimesById still holding the entry, so the indexes end up contradicting each other.
A different showtime can mean a different seat layout and start time entirely, so auto-moving tickets makes a decision for the user they never agreed to.
Rejecting the delete while active reservations exist, then removing the showtime only after cancellation and notification finish, avoids ever leaving a dangling reference.

scenario: 真实购票中用户选座后要花 30-60 秒支付，不能让别人抢走同一座位。
scenario_en: In real ticket checkout, a user may spend 30-60 seconds entering payment details after choosing seats, and no one else should take those seats.
q: 应加入哪种机制？
q_en: What mechanism should be added?
options: 临时 SeatHold，超时释放，付款成功转正式预订
支付前就永久创建 Reservation，失败也不释放
等支付成功那一刻才去检查座位是否还空
让用户截图证明自己先选中了这个座位
why: hold 把座位状态从二元变成 available/held/booked。它改善结账体验，但需要超时清理和确认流程。
why_en: Temporary holds protect selected seats during checkout and then either convert to reservations or lapse.
whenOtherWins: 如果支付被明确排除且 booking 是瞬时操作，基础 book() 不需要 hold。
options_en: A temporary SeatHold that lapses on timeout or confirms on payment.
Create a permanent Reservation upfront, never releasing it even if payment fails.
Check seat availability only at the moment payment succeeds.
Have the user screenshot proof they selected first.
tradeoff: 三态 hold 生命周期 vs 二元 available/booked 的结账体验风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 支付窗口内临时锁定座位的凭证，超时未确认会自动释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SeatHold is a temporary claim on a seat during checkout that auto-releases if it is never confirmed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户从选座到完成支付的整个流程窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Checkout is the window from selecting seats to completing payment.

optionExplanations: 选座后先进入一个短时 hold，把纯二元的座位占用拆成 available、held、booked 三档，超时没人确认就自动放回，付款成功再转成正式 Reservation。
支付一旦失败或用户中途放弃，座位就永久被占死，别人再也订不到，是最容易堆出死票的做法。
只在支付成功那一刻才检查，两人可能都先选了同一个座位再各自去支付，等真正撞车时才发现，体验很差。
截图不是系统能验证的凭据，也没法自动化处理并发，等于把该由代码保证的事情丢给人工核对。
optionExplanations_en: It turns seat state into a three-way available/held/booked lifecycle: a short-lived hold on selection that auto-releases on timeout, or converts into a Reservation once payment succeeds.
If payment fails or the user abandons checkout, the seat stays permanently claimed with no one able to book it — the easiest way to pile up dead tickets.
Checking only at the moment payment succeeds lets two users both select the same seat and only discover the conflict when one of them pays — a poor experience.
A screenshot isn't something the system can verify or use to resolve concurrency automatically — it just offloads a job the code should guarantee onto manual review.

scenario: 加入 10 分钟结账 hold 后，一个用户的 hold 已超时未确认，另一个用户正在选同一座位。
scenario_en: With a ten-minute checkout hold added, one user's hold has timed out unconfirmed while another user is picking that same seat.
q: 加入 temporary holds 后，isAvailable 应检查哪些状态？（多选）
q_en: After adding temporary holds, what states should isAvailable check? (select all that apply)
options: 是否被现有 Reservation 预订
是否被未过期 SeatHold 持有
是否被已过期 hold 持有
是否电影标题匹配
why: 已过期 hold 应清理或视为无效，不应继续占座。电影标题不参与单个座位的可用性判断。
why_en: Availability with holds must exclude booked seats and seats held by non-expired holds.
options_en: Whether an existing Reservation already booked it.
Whether a non-expired SeatHold is holding it.
Whether an expired hold is holding it.
Whether the movie title matches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超过 expiresAt 时间仍未被确认或清理的临时占位记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An expired hold is a temporary seat claim whose timeout has passed without being confirmed or cleaned up.

optionExplanations: 已经成立的 reservation 占用座位是最基本的检查，缺了这条双订就防不住。
还没到期的 hold 同样在占用座位，结账窗口内不检查它，两人可能同时选中同一个座位。
一个 hold 一旦过了它的有效期限，就不该继续占座——应该被当成可用座位处理，而不是拿去挡住新的预订。
isAvailable 问的是单个座位状态，跟电影标题完全无关，这条检查放错了维度。
optionExplanations_en: An existing reservation occupying the seat is the most basic check — skip it and double-booking is unstoppable.
A hold that hasn't lapsed yet is also occupying the seat; skip checking it during checkout and two users could land on the same seat at once.
Once a hold has lapsed past its window, it shouldn't keep blocking the seat — a lapsed hold should be treated as available again, not as still holding it.
isAvailable is about one seat's state; the movie title has nothing to do with it — this check is at the wrong dimension entirely.

q: 临时 hold 转正式预订的正确流程是什么？
q_en: What is the correct flow from temporary hold to confirmed reservation?
steps: holdSeats 在同一 Showtime 锁内确认座位可用并记录 expiresAt。
用户完成支付后提交 holdId。
confirmHold 检查 hold 存在且未过期。
删除 hold 并把 reservation 加入 reservations。
后台任务清理无人确认的过期 hold。
why: hold 和 booking 使用同一把 showtime 锁，可以防止 hold 与 reservation 互相穿插。过期清理防止座位永久锁住。
why_en: Seat holds share the showtime lock, confirm into reservations, and need cleanup for abandoned holds.
diagram:
stateDiagram
  [*] --> Available
  Available --> Held
  Held --> Booked: pay
  Held --> Available: timeout
  Booked --> Available: cancel

termDefinitions.meaning: 支付成功后把 hold 转换成正式 reservation 的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: confirmHold is the method that converts a valid hold into a confirmed reservation after payment succeeds.

scenario: 加入 hold 后，超时未确认的座位必须自动回到可订状态，非法转换要被挡住。
scenario_en: Once holds exist, a seat whose hold times out unconfirmed must return to bookable on its own, and illegal transitions must be blocked.
q: 文章为什么说 seat hold 引入的是小型状态生命周期？
q_en: Why does a seat hold introduce a small state lifecycle?
options: Movie 会经历从上映中变成已下映的状态转换
座位有 available/held/booked/released 四态
Theater 对象会在系统运行期间被直接替换成 Reservation 对象
Search 查询过程会直接变成支付流程的一部分
why: 一旦状态转换带规则，就要小心非法转换。三态时简单字段足够，状态继续增多时可以考虑 State pattern。
why_en: Seat holds introduce a lifecycle with available, held, booked, and released transitions.
options_en: A Movie transitions from currently showing to no longer showing.
A seat has explicit available/held/booked/released states.
A Theater object gets directly replaced by a Reservation object at runtime.
A Search query directly becomes part of the payment flow.
tradeoff: 小型状态生命周期用简单字段 vs 状态继续增多时改用 State pattern

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个状态建成独立对象、显式定义合法转换的设计模式，用于状态数增多变复杂时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The State pattern models each state as its own object with explicit legal transitions, useful once a lifecycle grows more states.

optionExplanations: 电影上映状态是产品层面的元数据变化，不是本题在讨论的、跟座位绑定的那套状态机。
座位加入 hold 后有 available、held、booked、released 四个状态，转换规则一多，就得防着中间被跳过走错状态，这正是所说的小型生命周期。
Theater 是持有 showtime 列表的容器，它的类型不会在运行期间被替换成另一个完全不同的类。
Search 是只读查询，支付是完全独立的后续流程，两者不会因为加了 hold 就合并成一个步骤。
optionExplanations_en: A movie's showing status is product-level metadata, not the seat-bound state machine this question is actually about.

Once holds exist, a seat cycles through available, held, booked, and released with explicit transition rules, and once transitions carry rules you must guard against illegal jumps — exactly the small lifecycle being described.
Theater is a container holding a list of showtimes; its type never gets swapped out for a completely different class at runtime.
Search is a read-only query and payment is a separate downstream flow — adding holds doesn't merge the two into one step.

scenario: 为 SeatHold 选择过期时间，用户需要输入支付信息。
scenario_en: You need to choose the expiration time for a SeatHold while users enter payment details.
q: 合理的设计判断是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable design judgment?
options: 无论场次冷热，全部场次都统一写死固定 1 秒超时
hold 一旦创建就必定永不失效
5-10 分钟常见，业务可调，过短伤用户过长占座
必须一直等到电影正式开场才失效
why: timeout 是业务权衡，不是固定算法常量。可用 Strategy 封装不同场景的超时策略，但基础设计可先用配置值。
why_en: Hold timeout is a business tradeoff between checkout usability and seat availability.
whenOtherWins: 高需求首映场可能使用更短 hold，低峰场次可以更宽松。
options_en: Hard-code the exact same fixed 1-second timeout for every showtime, hot or not.
Once created, a hold should absolutely never lapse.
5-10 minutes is typical and tunable, too short hurts users and too long locks seats.
A hold must wait all the way until the movie actually starts to lapse.
tradeoff: 结账可用时间 vs 座位被无谓锁住的时长

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段状态被允许维持的最长时间，超过就自动失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A timeout is the maximum duration a state is allowed to persist before it automatically expires.

optionExplanations: 不管场次冷热都写死 1 秒，连输入卡号都不够，用户还没填完支付信息 hold 就没了，等于变相拒绝所有正常结账。
hold 一旦创建就永不失效，用户中途放弃也会让座位永久锁死，其他人再也订不到。
超时时长本质是业务权衡：太短挤压用户填支付信息的时间，太长又让没人认领的座位白白占着，5-10 分钟是常见且可调的经验值。
等到开场才让 hold 失效，意味着一个放弃结账的用户能把座位锁到最后一刻，跟座位该尽快放出去矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Hard-coding 1 second regardless of demand isn't even enough to type in a card number — the hold would time out before the user finishes entering payment details, effectively blocking every normal checkout.
A hold that never times out means an abandoned checkout locks the seat forever, with no one else ever able to book it.

The timeout length is fundamentally a business tradeoff: too short squeezes the time users have to enter payment, too long leaves an unclaimed seat sitting idle — 5-10 minutes is a common, tunable rule of thumb.
Waiting until the movie starts to release the hold means an abandoned checkout can lock the seat all the way to showtime, fighting against freeing it back up quickly.

scenario: 一个线程在取消、另一个在预订同一场次，只有一个对象持有那把 synchronized 锁。
scenario_en: One thread cancels while another books the same showing, and only one object holds the synchronized lock.
q: 为什么不把 Reservation.cancel() 做成直接修改 Showtime？
q_en: Why shouldn't Reservation.cancel() directly modify Showtime?
options: Reservation 对象其实根本没有 confirmationId 字段
Showtime 设计上不应该知道任何 seatIds 信息
取消操作从设计上就不需要释放任何座位
Reservation 是记录，不该有权改 Showtime 的 list
why: 修改座位状态的权力留在 Showtime，能把并发控制集中在一个对象。Reservation 只携带取消所需数据。
why_en: Reservation is a record, while Showtime owns the mutable booking state and synchronization.
options_en: Reservation objects don't actually have a confirmationId field.
Showtime shouldn't know about any seatIds by design.
Cancellation doesn't need to free any seats by design.
Reservation is a record and shouldn't have write access to Showtime's list.
tradeoff: 状态修改权集中在 Showtime vs 分散到 Reservation 造成双写风险

termDefinitions.term: mutable state owner / 可变状态拥有者
termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一被允许修改某份状态的对象，其余对象只能通过它间接操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The mutable-state owner is the one object allowed to change a piece of state directly; everyone else must go through it.

optionExplanations: confirmationId 正是 reservationsById 索引和外部取消请求用的主键，Reservation 一直都有这个字段。
Showtime.book 恰恰要拿 seatIds 去做合法性和可用性校验，它必须知道座位信息才能完成预订。
取消的核心目的就是把座位从 reservations 里移除、还给别人订，不释放座位这件事本身就没有意义。
Reservation 只是携带取消所需数据的记录，真正能修改 reservations 列表的权限留在 Showtime 一处，能把并发控制集中管理。
optionExplanations_en: confirmationId is exactly the key used by reservationsById and by external cancel requests — Reservation has always carried that field.
Showtime.book specifically needs seatIds to run its validity and availability checks — it has to know about seats to complete a booking.
The entire point of cancellation is to remove the seats from reservations and give them back — a cancellation that frees no seats wouldn't do anything.
Reservation is just a record carrying the data cancellation needs; the actual permission to mutate the reservations list stays in one place, Showtime, keeping concurrency control centralized.

q: 补全索引维护代价：
q_en: Fill in the cost of maintaining lookup indexes.
text: showtimesById、moviesById、showtimesByMovieId 让读路径更快，但动态 add/remove 时必须保持这些{{派生索引}}和 theater.showtimes 的{{同步}}。
why: 这是所有 denormalized data 的共同代价。读性能提升换来写路径更容易出错。
why_en: Indexes speed reads but make writes responsible for keeping denormalized structures in sync.

termDefinitions.term: denormalized data / 反规范化数据
termDefinitions.meaning: 为读性能而额外保存的冗余数据副本，需要在写路径里手动保持同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalized data is a redundant copy kept purely for read speed, and the write path must manually keep it in sync.

scenario: 用户取消 reservation 的同时，另一个用户试图预订同一批座位。
scenario_en: One user cancels a reservation while another user tries to book the same seats.
q: 为什么 Showtime.cancel 也应该同步？
q_en: Why should Showtime.cancel also be synchronized?
options: 避免预订扫描到并发修改中的列表
因为每次取消都要重新搜索一遍电影
因为 synchronized 关键字会自动帮你退款
因为 Seat 是字符串，天生不支持删除操作
why: book 和 cancel 都读写同一 reservations 列表，必须使用同一并发边界。否则可能出现迭代和修改交错。
why_en: Cancel must synchronize with booking because both mutate the same reservations list.
options_en: It stops a booking from scanning the list mid-modification.
Because every cancellation has to re-search for the movie.
Because the synchronized keyword automatically issues a refund.
Because Seat is a string and strings can't be deleted.
tradeoff: book 和 cancel 共用同一把锁 vs 各自加锁导致读到中间状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个线程的操作步骤在时间上穿插执行，可能看到中间不一致的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving is when two threads' steps get mixed together in time, potentially exposing an inconsistent in-between state.

optionExplanations: 这两个操作（book、cancel）读写的是同一份 reservations 数据，不加锁就可能一边遍历一边删除交错，结果不可预期。
取消走的是 confirmationId 索引直接路由到 reservation，跟重新搜索电影完全无关。
synchronized 只负责保证同一时刻只有一个线程执行这段代码，退款是完全独立的业务逻辑，锁不会替你处理。
被删除的是列表里的 reservation 对象，不是 Seat 字符串本身，Seat 能不能删和这道题无关。
optionExplanations_en: book and cancel both read and write the same reservations list, so without a lock one thread could be iterating it while another deletes from it, giving unpredictable results.
Cancellation routes straight through the confirmationId index to the reservation — it has nothing to do with re-searching for the movie.
synchronized only guarantees one thread runs this code at a time; issuing a refund is completely separate business logic that the lock doesn't handle.
What gets removed is the reservation object inside the reservations list, not the Seat string itself — whether strings are deletable isn't the issue here.

scenario: 有人提议新增 Payment、SeatPrice、SeatType、RescheduleService。
scenario_en: Someone proposes adding Payment, SeatPrice, SeatType, and RescheduleService to the base model.
q: 基础需求下应该怎么回应？
q_en: How should you respond under the base requirements?
options: 把它们全部实现出来，显得设计很完整
指出它们被排除，先保持核心模型
不管职责边界，把它们都塞进 BookingSystem
干脆让 Movie 类顺便负责支付逻辑
why: LLD 面试要展示范围控制。超出需求的功能会分散注意力并增加不必要状态。
why_en: Scope control keeps the design focused on booking and cancellation rather than excluded features.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确加入支付、座位等级或改签，再扩展相应实体和状态机。
options_en: Implement all of them so the design looks complete.
Point out they're excluded and keep the core model as-is.
Ignore responsibility boundaries and cram them into BookingSystem.
Just make the Movie class handle payment on the side.
tradeoff: 守住需求边界 vs 抢答范围外功能分散设计精力

termDefinitions.meaning: 在没有被要求的情况下不断加功能，导致核心设计被稀释。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is adding unrequested features until the core design gets diluted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象、类和接口层面的系统详细设计，常见于工程面试的一种题型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD (Low-Level Design) is the detailed, class-and-interface-level design of a system, a common software engineering interview format.

optionExplanations: 面试官已经明确把支付、定价、改签排除在基础范围外，硬把它们都实现出来只会分散时间、稀释核心讨论。
先说明这些功能在需求里被明确排除，把精力留在核心模型上，展示的是范围控制能力，而不是回避问题。
把无关职责都塞进 BookingSystem 会让它从编排者变成什么都管的上帝对象，违反职责分离。
支付跟电影信息毫无关系，让 Movie 顺带管支付是把两个完全不相关的职责硬绑在一起。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer already explicitly excluded payment, pricing, and rescheduling from the base scope; forcing them in just burns time and dilutes the core discussion.
Naming these as explicitly out of scope and keeping focus on the core model demonstrates scope control, not avoidance.
Cramming unrelated responsibilities into BookingSystem turns it from an orchestrator into a god object that manages everything, breaking separation of concerns.
Payment has nothing to do with movie metadata, so tacking payment onto Movie forcibly couples two completely unrelated responsibilities.

scenario: 45 分钟 senior 级 LLD 面试，面试官已看完类图，正在追问并发下为什么不会双订。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute senior LLD interview the interviewer has seen your class diagram and is now pressing on why concurrency can't double-book.
q: Senior 级 BookMyShow 回答应主动覆盖哪些点？（多选）
q_en: What should a senior-level BookMyShow answer proactively cover? (select all that apply)
options: check-then-act 竞态
per-showtime vs per-seat locking
Reservation 到 Showtime 的 back-reference
临时 seat hold 如何复用同步模型
why: 高级回答的核心是并发和状态归属。只列类名不足以证明能防止双订。
why_en: Senior answers should cover race conditions, lock granularity, routing references, and temporary holds.
options_en: The check-then-act race condition.
Per-showtime versus per-seat locking.
The Reservation-to-Showtime back-reference.
How a temporary seat hold reuses the same synchronization model.
optionExplanations: 点出 check-then-act 竞态，说明能看到检查和写入之间没加锁会产生双订，这是并发正确性的核心风险。
对比 per-showtime 和 per-seat 锁，说明能权衡实现复杂度和吞吐量，而不是只会用一种粒度。
讲清 Reservation 到 Showtime 的反向引用，说明知道取消要怎么路由到状态拥有者，而不是靠全局扫描。
解释临时 hold 怎么复用同一把 showtime 锁，说明扩展功能时没有引入新的并发漏洞。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the check-then-act race shows you see that an unlocked gap between checking and writing causes double-booking — the core concurrency risk.
Comparing per-showtime and per-seat locking shows you can weigh implementation complexity against throughput, not just default to one granularity.
Explaining the Reservation-to-Showtime back-reference shows you know how cancellation routes to the state owner instead of relying on a global scan.
Explaining how a temporary hold reuses the same showtime lock shows the extension doesn't introduce a new concurrency hole.

q: 按顺序排列 BookMyShow 的主设计链路：
q_en: Put the main BookMyShow design reasoning chain in order.
steps: 把 Showtime 定为座位状态和并发锁的拥有者。
澄清搜索、浏览、固定布局、多座位 booking、取消和并发要求。
把 Seat/Screen 降级成字符串或字段，保留 Movie/Theater/Reservation。
BookingSystem 建立索引并负责路由。
Showtime.book 在锁内完成 all-or-nothing 校验和保存。
why: 从范围到实体裁剪，再到状态拥有者和并发边界，是这题的核心论证顺序。
why_en: The design chain moves from scope and entity pruning to Showtime-owned state, indexing, and atomic booking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从需求约束到实体裁剪、状态归属、并发边界的完整推理顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A decision chain is the full reasoning order from requirement constraints to entity pruning, state ownership, and the concurrency boundary.

scenario: 用户用已经取消过的 confirmationId 再次取消。
scenario_en: A user tries to cancel again with a confirmationId that has already been cancelled.
q: 基础设计如何处理？
q_en: How should the base design handle this?
options: 系统自动帮用户把刚才取消的那次 reservation 悄悄恢复回来
自动把这张票转移到下一场放映
reservationsById 查不到，报 NotFound
只把 seatIds 字段清空，其余不变
why: 取消成功后全局索引删除该 confirmationId，再次使用和随机 ID 一样不可用。无需额外 usedReservations 集合。
why_en: After cancellation removes the reservation index entry, repeated cancellation is treated as not found.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要求区分“已取消”和“不存在”，需要保留历史 reservation 状态或审计记录。
options_en: The system quietly restores the just-cancelled reservation for the user.
The ticket is automatically moved to the next showing.
reservationsById has no entry, so it returns NotFound / invalid.
Only the seatIds field gets cleared, everything else stays.
tradeoff: 复用已删除索引的天然拒绝 vs 额外维护一份已取消历史状态
optionExplanations: 取消成功后 reservationsById 里那条记录已经被删掉，系统没有留任何东西可以悄悄恢复给用户。
转到下一场放映是完全没出现过的新功能，基础设计的取消流程不会做这种事。
第一次取消已经把这个确认码从索引里删掉，再查同一个值跟查一个随机不存在的值没区别，自然是 NotFound。
reservation 对象在第一次取消时已经从索引和 showtime 的列表里一起消失，没有只清空 seatIds 的中间状态可以操作。
optionExplanations_en: Once cancellation succeeds, the entry in reservationsById is already deleted — there's nothing left for the system to quietly restore for the user.
Moving the ticket to the next showing is a feature that was never part of this design — the base cancellation flow doesn't do that.
The first cancellation already removed confirmationId from reservationsById, so looking it up again is indistinguishable from a random id that never existed — NotFound is correct.
The reservation object itself already disappeared from both the index and the showtime's list on the first cancellation — there's no in-between state where only seatIds gets cleared.

scenario: 单厅固定 546 座，前端每次打开座位图都调一次 getAvailableSeats。
scenario_en: A hall has a fixed 546 seats, and the client calls getAvailableSeats every time it opens the seat map.
q: getAvailableSeats 的复杂度为什么在基础设计中可接受？
q_en: Why is getAvailableSeats complexity acceptable in the base design?
options: 因为它不需要看 reservations
因为它只在系统启动时运行
因为 546 是 O(1) 但 reservations 不能扫描
固定布局只有 546 个座位，加上已订座位扫描，成本很小
why: 固定布局扫描是常数级，reservation 数量也有限。为它维护更多长期状态未必值得。
why_en: A fixed 546-seat layout and modest reservation counts make derived availability cheap enough.
options_en: Because it never has to look at reservations.
Because it only runs once at system startup.
Because 546 is O(1) but reservations cannot be scanned.
The fixed layout is only 546 seats, plus scanning booked seats, so cost stays tiny.
tradeoff: 常数级布局扫描可接受 vs 为已订座位单独维护更多长期状态

termDefinitions.term: constant-size scan / 常数规模扫描
termDefinitions.meaning: 扫描的数据量有固定上限，不随用户量或时间增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A constant-size scan has a fixed upper bound on data volume that doesn't grow with users or time.

optionExplanations: getAvailableSeats 恰恰要看 reservations 来算出哪些座位已经被订走，不看它就没法排除已订座位。
这是一个查询方法，每次前端要渲染座位图都会调用它，不是只在系统启动时跑一次。
reservations 同样是可以扫描的——它的规模跟座位数一样有限，问题不在能不能扫，而在两者规模都够小。
布局固定在 546 个座位，reservations 数量也不会超过这个上限，两次扫描加起来仍是常数级，成本可以接受。
optionExplanations_en: getAvailableSeats specifically needs to look at reservations to figure out which seats are already taken — skip it and there's no way to exclude booked seats.
This is a query method the client calls every time it needs to render the seat map, not something that runs once at startup.
Reservations can be scanned too — their size is bounded by the same seat count, so the issue was never whether scanning is allowed, it's that both are small enough.
The layout is fixed at 546 seats, and reservations can't exceed that bound either, so both scans together stay constant-size and cheap enough to accept.

scenario: 面试最后要你总结这个系统最关键的不变量。
scenario_en: At the end of the interview, you need to summarize the key invariant of this system.
q: 哪一个最准确？
q_en: Which statement is most accurate?
options: 一个座位最多属于一份 active reservation
同一部 movie 在同一天只能在一家 theater 排片上映
每个 theater 永远只能有一个 screen
每个 user 一次最多只能订一个座位
why: 所有并发控制都服务于这个不变量。book 的锁和 all-or-nothing 校验就是为了保证座位不会双订。
why_en: The central invariant is that a seat within one showtime appears in at most one active reservation.
whenOtherWins: 加入 hold 后，应扩展为一个 seatId 最多处于一个 active reservation 或未过期 hold 中。
options_en: A seat belongs to at most one active reservation.
The same movie can only be scheduled at one theater on a given day.
A theater can only ever have one screen.
A user can only book one seat at a time.
tradeoff: 座位唯一占用不变量 vs 加 hold 后要扩展成 reservation-or-hold

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须保持为真的规则，所有操作都要维护它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a rule that must remain true at every point in time, and every operation has to preserve it.

optionExplanations: book 时的整单校验和加的锁、cancel 里的同步删除，全都是在维护这一条：同一场次内一个座位不会同时属于两份预订。
一部电影完全可以在同一天于多家影院同时排片，这跟本题的并发和座位不变量没有关系。
本设计并没有限制每个 theater 只能有一个 screen，实际上一个 theater 通常持有多场不同 showtime。
多座位一次预订本身就是明确要支持的能力（如 A5/A6/A7 一起订），一次一个座位并不是这道题的约束。
optionExplanations_en: Every lock and all-or-nothing check in book, and the synchronized removal in cancel, all exist to protect exactly this: within one showing, a seat never belongs to two active reservations at once.
A movie can absolutely be scheduled at multiple theaters on the same day — that has nothing to do with this design's concurrency or seat invariant.
Nothing in this design limits a theater to one screen; in practice a theater holds many different showtimes.
Booking several seats at once is explicitly a supported capability here (like A5/A6/A7 together) — one-seat-at-a-time was never a constraint of this design.

scenario: 改用 per-seat 锁后，座位状态同时存在 seat.bookedBy 和 showtime.reservations 两处。cancel 只清了 bookedBy。
scenario_en: After switching to per-seat locks, seat state lives in two places: seat.bookedBy and showtime.reservations. Cancel only clears bookedBy.
q: 这次漏改会让系统表现成什么样？
q_en: What does this missed update make the system look like?
options: 座位图显示已被订，但 book 该座位仍会成功
两个 reservation 同时指向该座位并双双确认成功
cancel 会直接抛 SeatUnavailableException 失败
座位立刻回到可订池，只是确认号索引里多一条垃圾
options_en: The seat map shows it as taken, yet booking that seat still succeeds.
Two reservations point at the same seat and both get confirmed.
Cancel itself fails with a SeatUnavailableException.
The seat returns to the pool right away, just leaving junk in the confirmation index.
why: per-seat 锁把座位状态拆成两份：bookedBy 决定能否加锁写入，reservations 决定座位图和可用性；漏同步一处，二者就长期分歧。
why_en: Per-seat locking splits seat state in two: bookedBy gates the write, while the reservations list drives the seat map, so missing one update leaves them permanently out of sync.
optionExplanations: book 只看 bookedBy（已清空）就放行，座位图只看 reservations（旧条目还在）。
双订要两个线程同时通过 bookedBy 检查，这里锁仍然是好的。
cancel 不做可用性校验，它只删除，异常出在后面的 book。
座位没回到池里，getAvailableSeats 仍从 reservations 推导。
optionExplanations_en: Book only reads bookedBy, which is now null, while the seat map only reads reservations, where the stale entry remains.
Double booking needs two threads to pass the bookedBy check at once; the lock itself is still working correctly here.
Cancel performs no availability check, it just deletes; the exception surfaces later in book.
The seat does not return to the pool, because getAvailableSeats still derives availability from the reservations list.

termDefinitions.meaning: per-seat 锁方案里挂在每个 Seat 对象上的字段，指向占用它的 Reservation，为空表示可订。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In the per-seat locking design, bookedBy is a field on each Seat object pointing at the reservation that owns it, and null means the seat is free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个座位一把独立的锁，只有抢同一座位的请求才互相阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-seat locking gives every seat its own lock, so only requests competing for the same seat block each other.

scenario: per-seat 锁方案下，用户取消一份含 A5、A6、A7 的预订，需要清掉这三个座位的 bookedBy。
scenario_en: Under per-seat locking, a user cancels a reservation covering A5, A6 and A7, so all three seats' bookedBy fields must be cleared.
q: cancel 应该怎么拿锁？
q_en: How should cancel acquire its locks?
options: 按排序后的 seatId 顺序重新获取这三把座位锁
只锁 reservations 列表，座位锁可以不拿
退回整场次的 synchronized 锁来做取消
按当初提交 seatIds 的原始顺序重新获取三把座位锁
options_en: Re-acquire all three seat locks in sorted seat-id order.
Lock only the reservations list and skip the seat locks.
Fall back to the whole-showtime synchronized lock for cancellation.
Re-acquire the three seat locks in the original submission order of the seat ids.
why: 取消要写 bookedBy 就必须持有对应座位锁，且顺序要和 book 一样按 seatId 排序；代价是 cancel 从一次列表删除变成一轮多锁获取与释放。
why_en: Cancel writes bookedBy, so it has to hold those seat locks, and it must take them in the same sorted order book uses, which turns a one-line delete into a full multi-lock round trip.
tradeoff: per-seat 换来的吞吐 vs cancel 也要走排序多锁获取
whenOtherWins: 回到 per-showtime 锁后，cancel 只需要一个 synchronized 块加一次列表删除。
optionExplanations: 写 bookedBy 属于状态修改，必须在锁内；排序保证与 book 同序。
bookedBy 是另一份状态，不拿座位锁清它就会和 book 抢同一字段。
per-seat 方案里已经没有整场次锁，混用两种粒度会失去互斥。
原始提交顺序因人而异，A→B 与 B→A 交叉就是死锁的经典形状。
optionExplanations_en: Clearing bookedBy is a state mutation, so it must happen under the lock, and sorting keeps cancel in the same order as book.
bookedBy is a separate piece of state; clearing it without the seat lock races directly against book writing the same field.
The per-seat design no longer has a whole-showtime lock, and mixing two granularities loses mutual exclusion entirely.
Submission order differs between callers, and A-then-B crossing B-then-A is the textbook shape of a deadlock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个线程各持有对方还需要的锁，谁都无法继续，只能一直互相等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock happens when two threads each hold a lock the other still needs, so neither can ever make progress.

termDefinitions.term: sorted lock ordering / 锁排序获取
termDefinitions.meaning: 所有线程都按同一个全局顺序获取多把锁，从而消除环形等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sorted lock ordering means every thread acquires multiple locks in the same global order, which removes any circular wait.

scenario: per-seat book 已按序拿下 A5、A6、A7 三把锁，随后发现 A6 的 bookedBy 非空，要抛 SeatUnavailableException。
scenario_en: A per-seat book has already taken the A5, A6 and A7 locks in order, then finds A6's bookedBy is non-null and must throw SeatUnavailableException.
q: 少写 finally 释放锁会怎样？
q_en: What happens if the finally block that releases the locks is missing?
options: A5、A6、A7 三把锁再也不会释放，这三个座位永久卡死
异常会被吞掉，用户拿到一个空的确认号
只有 A6 这把锁泄漏，A5 和 A7 会被自动回收
JVM 会在方法返回时自动释放所有已获取的显式锁，因此无影响
