options_en: None of the three locks are ever released, so those seats are wedged forever.
The exception gets swallowed and the user receives an empty confirmation id.
Only the A6 lock leaks, while A5 and A7 are reclaimed automatically.
The JVM automatically releases every explicit lock when the method returns, so nothing bad happens.
why: 抛异常时锁已经拿在手上，只有 finally 能无条件释放；否则后面任何人再订这三个座位都会永久阻塞在第一把锁上。
why_en: The locks are already held when the exception fires, and only a finally block releases them unconditionally, otherwise every later booking for those seats blocks forever on the first lock.
optionExplanations: 锁在 try 之前获取，异常绕过 release，三把锁一起泄漏。
异常照常向上抛给 BookingSystem，问题不在异常传播。
泄漏的是全部已获取的锁，不只是抛异常的那一把。
显式 Lock 不像 synchronized 会随栈帧退出自动释放，这正是要写 finally 的原因。
optionExplanations_en: The locks are taken before the try block, so the exception skips every release call and all three leak together.
The exception still propagates up to BookingSystem, so exception handling is not where this breaks.
Every already-acquired lock leaks, not only the one whose seat triggered the exception.
An explicit Lock is not released when the stack frame unwinds the way synchronized is, which is exactly why finally is required.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无论正常返回还是抛异常，finally 里的清理代码都保证执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A try/finally block guarantees the cleanup code runs whether the method returns normally or throws.

termDefinitions.meaning: 需要手动 acquire 和 release 的锁对象，不随代码块结束自动释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An explicit lock is a lock object you acquire and release by hand; it is not released automatically when a block exits.

scenario: isAvailable 和 getAvailableSeats 只读 reservations、不改任何状态，同时另一个线程正在 book 里往这个列表追加。
scenario_en: isAvailable and getAvailableSeats only read the reservations list and mutate nothing, while another thread is appending to that same list inside book.
q: 只读方法在无锁下的真实风险是什么？
q_en: What is the real risk of leaving these read-only methods unlocked?
options: 可能读到写入中途的列表，返回一份不一致的可用座位
完全安全，因为它们不修改任何状态
会导致双订，因为读操作没有排他性
会让正在 book 的线程读到一半的 reservation 而回滚整单预订
options_en: They can read a list mid-write and return an inconsistent set of available seats.
They are completely safe because they never modify state.
They cause double booking, since reads are not exclusive.
They make the booking thread read a half-written reservation and roll back the whole booking.
why: 不改状态只保证读方不破坏数据，不保证读到一致快照；双订的防线在 book 的整段临界区，读到旧值最多让座位图短暂过时。
why_en: Not mutating state only means the reader cannot corrupt anything; it does not guarantee a consistent snapshot, so a stale read just shows a briefly outdated seat map.
tradeoff: 只读免锁的吞吐 vs 座位图可能短暂过时
whenOtherWins: 若结算页要求座位图强一致，就把读也放进同一个 synchronized 块。
optionExplanations: 在列表追加过程中扫描，可能漏算刚写入的那份预订。
不修改不等于读到一致快照，写方中途的状态照样会被看到。
双订源于 book 的检查-写入竞态，和读方法无关。
book 的原子性由它自己的锁保证，外部读线程无法让它回滚。
optionExplanations_en: Scanning while an append is in flight can miss the reservation that was just written.
Not mutating is not the same as seeing a consistent snapshot; a writer's intermediate state is still visible.
Double booking comes from the check-then-act race inside book and has nothing to do with reads.
Book's atomicity is guaranteed by its own lock, and an outside reader cannot make it roll back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读到的是某一个时间点上完整的状态，而不是写入中途的半成品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consistent snapshot is state as it existed at one single instant, rather than a half-finished write.

scenario: 面试官确认 browse movies 只是电影标题的简单文本匹配，目录只有几百部电影且全在内存里。
scenario_en: The interviewer confirms that browsing movies means simple text matching on the title, with only a few hundred movies held in memory.
q: 搜索该怎么实现？
q_en: How should search be implemented?
options: 遍历内存里的 movie 索引做标题子串匹配
建倒排索引，把标题分词后按词查倒排表
接 Elasticsearch，交给它做分词、模糊匹配和排名
给 title 建前缀树以支持 typeahead 自动补全
options_en: Scan the in-memory movie index and do a substring match on the title.
Build an inverted index, tokenize titles and look terms up in the postings list.
Bring in Elasticsearch and let it handle tokenization, fuzzy matching and ranking.
Build a prefix trie over titles to support typeahead autocomplete.
why: 几百条数据的线性扫描是微秒级；倒排索引和 Elasticsearch 解决的是模糊、排名和海量文档，而这些需求已被面试官明确排除。
why_en: A linear scan over a few hundred titles takes microseconds, and inverted indexes or Elasticsearch solve fuzzy matching, ranking and huge corpora, all of which the interviewer explicitly ruled out.
tradeoff: 线性扫描零依赖 vs 目录变大后撑不起模糊与排名
whenOtherWins: 需求扩到拼写容错、按热度排名或百万级目录时，就该换成全文检索引擎。
optionExplanations: 一次标题 contains 判断，几百部电影扫完只要微秒级。
分词倒排是为词级检索和海量文档准备的，子串匹配用不上。
引入一个外部服务和索引同步链路，换来本题不需要的能力。
前缀树只能前缀命中，搜 ception 就找不到 Inception。
optionExplanations_en: A single contains check over a few hundred titles finishes in microseconds.
Tokenized inverted indexes exist for term-level retrieval over large corpora, which substring matching never needs.
It adds an external service plus an index-sync pipeline in exchange for capabilities this problem does not want.
A trie only matches prefixes, so searching for ception would never find Inception.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词映射到包含该词的文档列表的结构，是全文检索的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the list of documents containing it, and it is the basis of full-text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于倒排索引的分布式搜索引擎，提供分词、模糊匹配和相关性排名。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a distributed search engine built on inverted indexes that provides tokenization, fuzzy matching and relevance ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字符逐层分叉的树，能快速找出所有以某段前缀开头的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a character-by-character tree that quickly finds every string starting with a given prefix.

scenario: searchMovies 只对用户输入做了 toLowerCase，movie.getTitle() 原样参与 contains 比较，目录里存的是 Inception。
scenario_en: searchMovies lowercases the user's input but feeds movie.getTitle() into contains unchanged, and the catalog stores the title as Inception.
q: 用户搜 inception 会发生什么？
q_en: What happens when a user searches for inception?
options: 返回空，标题里没有全小写的子串
照常命中，contains 本身就忽略大小写
抛异常，大小写不同的字符串无法比较
命中但被排到结果末尾，算作低优先匹配
options_en: It returns nothing, because the title contains no all-lowercase substring.
It matches fine, since contains ignores case on its own.
It throws, because strings of differing case cannot be compared.
It matches but lands at the end of the results as a low-priority hit.
why: contains 是区分大小写的逐字符比较，必须两边都 toLowerCase 才能对齐；只降一边等于把所有大小写不同的查询静默搜空。
why_en: contains is a case-sensitive character comparison, so both sides must be lowercased; folding only one side silently returns nothing for every differently-cased query.
optionExplanations: Inception 里找不到 inception 这个子串，整条结果被过滤掉。
标准字符串 contains 逐字符比较，大小写不同即不相等。
比较不会抛异常，只会安静地返回 false，这才是它难查的原因。
本设计没有相关性排序，命中就直接进结果列表。
optionExplanations_en: Inception does not contain the substring inception, so the row is filtered out entirely.
A standard string contains compares character by character, and different cases are simply not equal.
The comparison never throws; it quietly returns false, which is exactly what makes this bug hard to spot.
This design has no relevance ordering at all, so a hit goes straight into the result list.

termDefinitions.term: case-insensitive matching / 忽略大小写匹配
termDefinitions.meaning: 比较前把查询和被查内容统一转成同一种大小写，使两者能对齐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Case-insensitive matching normalizes both the query and the target to the same case before comparing them.

scenario: 同一个 Movie 对象被三家影院的十几个 Showtime 共同引用，多个线程会并发读它的 title。
scenario_en: One Movie object is referenced by a dozen Showtimes across three theaters, and many threads read its title concurrently.
q: Movie 该不该提供 setter？
q_en: Should Movie expose setters?
options: 不提供，只暴露 getter 让它天然不可变
提供 setTitle，改片名时一处生效很方便
提供 setter，但给每个字段加 synchronized 保护
提供 setter，并让 Movie 通知所有引用它的 Showtime 刷新缓存
options_en: No setters, only getters, so the object is immutable by construction.
Add setTitle, so renaming a film takes effect everywhere from one place.
Add setters but guard every field with synchronized.
Add setters and have Movie notify every Showtime referencing it to refresh its cache.
why: 共享引用一旦可变，一处改动就会悄悄改掉十几个 showtime 看到的片名；不可变让它免锁共享，代价是改名只能换一个新 Movie 对象。
why_en: Once a shared reference is mutable, one edit silently rewrites what a dozen showtimes display, so immutability buys lock-free sharing at the cost of replacing the object to rename a film.
tradeoff: 不可变对象免锁共享 vs 改名只能整体替换对象
whenOtherWins: 若片名要支持后台实时编辑，就得引入可变字段并为并发读写加保护。
optionExplanations: 没有写入点就没有并发写问题，引用方也看不到半改状态。
一处生效正是风险所在：所有引用方被无声地改掉。
加锁能保证单次写原子，读方仍会在两次读之间看到片名变化。
本设计里 Showtime 并不缓存片名，通知链路是为不存在的问题加复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: With no write path there is no concurrent write problem, and no reader can observe a half-updated object.
Taking effect everywhere is precisely the danger: every referencing showtime is changed without knowing.
Locking makes each write atomic, but a reader can still see the title change between two consecutive reads.
Showtime never caches the title in this design, so a notification chain adds complexity for a problem that does not exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构造后所有字段都不再改变的对象，可以被任意线程安全共享。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An immutable object never changes after construction, so any number of threads can share it safely.

scenario: 需求追加：Movie 要带上 duration、genre、rating 三个字段供前端展示，预订流程本身完全不变。
scenario_en: New requirement: Movie must carry duration, genre and rating for the UI to display, while the booking flow itself is unchanged.
q: 改动范围应该有多大？
q_en: How far should this change reach?
options: 只改 Movie 的字段和构造函数
Movie 加字段，同时给 Showtime 加对应的透传方法
Movie 加字段，并在 BookingSystem 建 genre 和 rating 索引
把三个字段拆成独立的 MovieMetadata 类并让 Showtime 持有它
options_en: Only Movie's fields and constructor change.
Add the fields to Movie plus matching pass-through getters on Showtime.
Add the fields to Movie and build genre and rating indexes on BookingSystem.
Split the three fields into a separate MovieMetadata class that Showtime holds.
why: booking flow 只用 movie.getId() 路由、用 title 搜索，新字段没有任何调用方，改动止步于 Movie；代价是前端要多走一次 getMovie() 才拿得到。
why_en: The booking flow only routes on movie id and searches on title, so the new fields have no callers and the change stops at Movie, at the cost of one extra getMovie hop for the UI.
tradeoff: 字段内聚在 Movie vs 新增查询维度时要另建索引
whenOtherWins: 一旦需求变成按 genre 筛选场次，就必须回到 BookingSystem 建索引。
optionExplanations: Showtime 已持有 Movie 引用，前端顺着取即可，不需要新链路。
透传方法只是把同一份数据再抄一遍接口，扩大要同步的表面积。
没有按 genre 或 rating 查询的需求前，索引是纯维护成本。
拆类多一次解引用，而这三个字段本来就属于电影自身的身份。
optionExplanations_en: Showtime already holds a Movie reference, so the UI can follow it and no new path is needed.
Pass-through getters just copy the same data onto a second interface, widening the surface you must keep in sync.
Until something actually queries by genre or rating, those indexes are pure maintenance cost.
Splitting the class adds a dereference, and these three fields are part of the film's own identity anyway.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对扩展开放、对修改关闭：加新能力时尽量只新增代码，不改已有调用方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The open-closed principle says new capability should be added by extension rather than by editing existing callers.

scenario: Showtime 持有 theater 引用，Theater 持有 showtimes 列表，两边互指；运行时的预订和取消只动 Showtime。
scenario_en: Showtime holds a theater reference and Theater holds a list of showtimes, pointing at each other, while runtime booking and cancellation only touch Showtime.
q: Showtime 的 theater 引用能用来做什么？
q_en: What is Showtime's theater reference actually for?
options: 只做导航：从 reservation 回溯到影院展示
由 Showtime 通过它把自己加进 theater.showtimes
预订时用它反向锁住整个 theater 保证一致
取消时用它把 showtime 从 theater 列表里摘掉
options_en: Navigation only: walk from a reservation back to the theater to display it.
Let Showtime use it to add itself into theater.showtimes.
Use it during booking to lock the whole theater for consistency.
Use it during cancellation to remove the showtime from the theater's list.
why: Theater 是 aggregate root，结构性变更只从它那一侧发起；这条双向链接在 setup 时建立一次之后不再变，避免两侧各改一半。
why_en: Theater is the aggregate root, so structural changes only originate on its side, and the bidirectional link is wired once during setup and never mutated again.
tradeoff: 单侧维护结构的简单 vs 导航方向上多存一个引用
whenOtherWins: 若场次可以在影院之间迁移，就得指定唯一写入口并显式同步另一侧。
optionExplanations: reservation → showtime → theater 一路取到影院名给用户看。
构造顺序恰恰相反：调用方先建 Theater，再把 Showtime 挂上去。
锁粒度是单个 showtime，锁整个影院会把不相干的场次全排队。
摘除由 BookingSystem.removeShowtime 统一发起，不由 Showtime 自己动。
optionExplanations_en: It lets you walk reservation to showtime to theater and show the user where their booking is.
The construction order is the opposite: the caller creates the Theater first and then attaches Showtimes to it.
Locking granularity is a single showtime; locking a whole theater would queue up completely unrelated screenings.
Removal is driven centrally by BookingSystem.removeShowtime, not by a Showtime detaching itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组关联对象的唯一入口，外部只能通过它修改这组对象的结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregate root is the single entry point through which outside code may change the structure of a cluster of related objects.

scenario: Theater 需要一份 showtimes 列表，Showtime 构造又要一个 theater 引用，两个类互相需要对方先存在。
scenario_en: Theater needs a list of showtimes while constructing a Showtime needs a theater reference, so each class needs the other to exist first.
q: 构造顺序应该怎么排？
q_en: How should the construction order be arranged?
options: Theater 先构造出空列表，再逐个挂上 Showtime
先构造全部 Showtime，再用它们构造 Theater
把 theater 引用改成延迟解析的 theaterId 字符串
在 Theater 构造函数里同时创建它名下的全部 Showtime 对象
options_en: Construct Theater with an empty list first, then attach Showtimes one by one.
Construct all the Showtimes first, then build the Theater from them.
Replace the theater reference with a lazily resolved theaterId string.
Create all of the theater's Showtime objects inside the Theater constructor itself.
why: Theater 的 showtimes 初始化为空列表就切断了环：对象先存在、关系后建立；代价是 Theater 有一小段还没挂上场次的中间状态。
why_en: Initializing Theater's showtimes to an empty list breaks the cycle: objects exist first and relationships are wired afterwards, at the cost of a brief window where the theater has no showtimes yet.
optionExplanations: 构造函数只置 id、name 和空列表，Showtime 拿到引用后再 add 进来。
Showtime 构造时就要 theater 引用，那时 Theater 还不存在。
改成 id 确实能断环，但每次导航都要回 BookingSystem 查表。
Showtime 仍需把已构造好的 Theater 传进去，环并没有真正解开。
optionExplanations_en: The constructor only sets id, name and an empty list; each Showtime is added after it receives the reference.
A Showtime needs the theater reference at construction time, and at that moment the Theater does not exist yet.
Using an id does break the cycle, but every navigation then has to look the theater up in BookingSystem.
Each Showtime still needs a fully constructed Theater passed in, so the cycle is not actually broken.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个对象各自需要对方先存在才能构造，必须靠先建空壳再补关系来打破。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circular dependency is when two objects each need the other to exist first, and it is broken by constructing one empty and wiring the link afterwards.

scenario: 产品要改预订规则：每份预订最多 6 个座位，且开场前 10 分钟停止售票。
scenario_en: Product changes the booking rules: at most six seats per reservation, and sales close ten minutes before showtime.
q: 这次改动要碰哪些类？
q_en: Which classes does this change have to touch?
options: 只改 Showtime 的 book 校验
改 Showtime 的 book，并在 Theater 加同样的校验兜底
改 BookingSystem.book，让统一入口拦截
在 Theater 上加规则，由它在转发预订前校验
options_en: Only the validation inside Showtime.book.
Change Showtime.book and add the same check on Theater as a safety net.
Change BookingSystem.book so the single entry point rejects it.
Put the rule on Theater and have it validate before forwarding the booking.
why: Theater 只是场次容器、完全不参与预订，所以座位规则全部收敛在 Showtime 一处；代价是要分清入口的参数校验和实体的业务校验各管什么。
why_en: Theater is only a container and takes no part in booking, so every seat rule converges on Showtime, provided you keep entry-point input validation distinct from entity business rules.
tradeoff: 规则单点收敛 vs 入口层与实体层的校验职责要划清
whenOtherWins: 若规则是影院级的（比如整馆临时停售），才该由 Theater 这一层承载。
optionExplanations: 座位数和售票截止都要看这一场的状态，只有 Showtime 手上有。
两处同样的校验必然漂移，改漏一处就是线上不一致。
入口只该做参数合法性；业务规则放这里会绕过 Showtime 的锁。
Theater 不转发预订，BookingSystem 通过 showtimesById 直达场次。
optionExplanations_en: Both the seat count and the cutoff depend on this screening's own state, which only Showtime holds.
Two copies of the same check will drift apart, and forgetting one of them is a production inconsistency.
The entry point should only validate inputs; putting business rules here bypasses Showtime's lock.
Theater does not forward bookings at all; BookingSystem reaches the showtime directly through showtimesById.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类只承担一类变化原因，规则改动时只需要改一个地方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single responsibility means a class has one reason to change, so a rule change only edits one place.

scenario: 纯内存实现跑了半年，每家影院每天新增 8 场，过期场次从未移除，getShowtimesAtTheater 每次都要遍历全部场次。
scenario_en: The pure in-memory design has run for half a year, each theater adds eight screenings a day, expired ones are never removed, and getShowtimesAtTheater walks the whole list every call.
q: 长期运行下要补上哪一条？
q_en: What must be added for this to survive long-running operation?
options: 定期清理已过期的 showtime
给 getShowtimesAtTheater 加一层结果缓存
把 showtimes 换成按开场时间排序的跳表
限制每家影院最多保留 1000 个 showtime 对象
options_en: Periodically purge expired showtimes.
Add a result cache in front of getShowtimesAtTheater.
Replace the list with a skip list ordered by start time.
Cap each theater at a maximum of 1000 retained showtime objects.
why: 过期场次既不可订也不会被引用，却持续占内存并拖慢每次遍历；生产上换成数据库后由查询条件天然规避，纯内存版必须显式加清理任务。
why_en: Expired showtimes are neither bookable nor referenced, yet they keep consuming memory and slowing every scan, so an in-memory design needs an explicit cleanup job that a database query would give you for free.
optionExplanations: 开场时间已过的场次可以整批移出索引，内存和遍历成本一起降。
缓存挡不住列表本身变长，任何一次写入都要全量失效。
排序结构只让过滤更快，垃圾对象仍然全部留在内存里。
硬上限会在影院正常排片时误删还没上映的未来场次。
optionExplanations_en: Screenings whose start time has passed can be dropped from the indexes in bulk, cutting both memory and scan cost.
A cache cannot stop the underlying list from growing, and any write invalidates the whole thing.
An ordered structure only makes filtering faster; the garbage objects all still sit in memory.
A hard cap would evict future screenings that have not even played yet during normal scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后台任务定期移除已经无用的对象，避免内存和遍历成本单向增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Expiry cleanup is a background job that periodically removes objects that are no longer useful, so memory and scan cost stop growing forever.

scenario: 运营在高峰期临时加一场；同一时刻已有几十个线程正在别的 showtime 里跑 synchronized 的 book。
scenario_en: Operations adds a late screening at peak time, while dozens of threads are already inside synchronized book calls on other showtimes.
q: addShowtime 该怎么加锁？
q_en: How should addShowtime be synchronized?
options: 对 BookingSystem 的索引结构加写锁
复用某一个 Showtime 的 synchronized 块
给全系统加一把大锁，预订和加场次共用
不用加锁，新场次还没有任何预订不会冲突
options_en: Take a write lock on BookingSystem's index structures.
Reuse the synchronized block of one of the Showtimes.
Add one global lock shared by booking and by adding showtimes.
No lock is needed, since a new showtime has no reservations to conflict with.
why: addShowtime 改的是 showtimesById、showtimesByMovieId 这类共享索引，需要写锁；预订并发仍由各 Showtime 自己的 synchronized 承担，两层锁互不重叠。
why_en: addShowtime mutates shared indexes like showtimesById, so it needs a write lock, while booking concurrency stays on each Showtime's own synchronized block and the two layers never overlap.
tradeoff: 结构写锁 vs 场次内预订锁：两层粒度各管各的
whenOtherWins: 若索引换成并发安全的 map，结构写锁可以退化成无锁写入。
optionExplanations: 并发写 map 会破坏索引结构，读者可能拿到半建好的桶。
别的 Showtime 的锁保护不了 BookingSystem 的字段，粒度对不上。
一把大锁会让所有预订串到加场次后面，白白丢掉吞吐。
新场次确实没有预订，但索引本身正被其它线程并发读。
optionExplanations_en: Concurrent map writes can corrupt the index structure, and a reader may observe a half-built bucket.
Another Showtime's lock protects nothing on BookingSystem; the granularity simply does not line up.
A single global lock serializes every booking behind the schedule change and throws away throughput for nothing.
The new showtime has no reservations, but the indexes themselves are being read concurrently right now.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读写锁中的排他一侧，持有期间禁止其它读写，用于结构性修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write lock is the exclusive side of a read-write lock, blocking all other readers and writers while a structural change is made.

scenario: removeShowtime 已从 showtimesById 和 showtimesByMovieId 删掉了场次，却忘了从 theater.getShowtimes() 里移除。
scenario_en: removeShowtime already deleted the screening from showtimesById and showtimesByMovieId, but forgot to remove it from theater.getShowtimes().
q: 会出现哪些现象？（多选）
q_en: Which symptoms show up? (multiple)
options: 影院页面仍列出该场次，点进去预订报 ShowtimeNotFound
按电影标题搜索仍会返回这一场
cleanupMovieIndex 认为电影还在上映而保留在搜索索引
该影院其它场次的预订都会失败
options_en: The theater page still lists the screening, and booking it returns ShowtimeNotFound.
Searching by movie title still returns this screening.
cleanupMovieIndex concludes the film is still showing and keeps it in the search index.
Bookings for all the theater's other screenings start failing.
why: 场次同时挂在三处结构上：一处按 id 路由预订、一处支撑标题搜索、一处支撑影院页面展示；漏清一处就留下悬挂引用，用户看得见却订不了。
why_en: A screening lives in three structures at once, one for routing, one for search and one for display, so missing any of them leaves a dangling reference users can see but cannot book.
optionExplanations: 浏览走 theater.showtimes，预订走 showtimesById，两条路径不再一致。
搜索走 showtimesByMovieId，那一处已经清干净了。
它遍历各影院的 showtimes 找残留引用，一命中就提前返回保留电影。
其它场次各自在索引里，不受这条残留引用影响。
optionExplanations_en: Browsing reads theater.showtimes while booking reads showtimesById, and the two paths no longer agree.
Search goes through showtimesByMovieId, and that index was cleaned up correctly.
It walks each theater's showtimes looking for remaining references, and one hit makes it return early and keep the film.
Every other screening still sits in the indexes and is unaffected by this leftover reference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个结构还指向已被逻辑删除的对象，导致两条访问路径给出矛盾结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dangling reference is a structure still pointing at a logically deleted object, making two access paths disagree.

scenario: AMC 的《Inception》最后一场被删掉，但同城另一家影院明天还排了两场《Inception》。
scenario_en: The last Inception screening at AMC is removed, but another theater in the same city still has two Inception screenings tomorrow.
q: 该不该把这部电影移出索引？
q_en: Should the film be pulled from the index?
options: 不该，先遍历确认没有场次再引用它才能删
该删，删场次时顺手把它的 movie 一起清掉
该删，用户搜不到时再按需重建索引
不该删，movie 索引一旦建立就永远保留
options_en: No, only delete after scanning to confirm no screening still references it.
Yes, clear the movie along with the screening in one step.
Yes, and rebuild the index on demand when a user's search misses.
No, once a movie is in the index it stays there forever.
why: moviesById 和 showtimesByMovieId 是全系统共享的，只要还有任何一场引用这部电影就必须留着；代价是这次确认要全扫影院与场次，好在只在删除时跑。
why_en: The movie indexes are shared system-wide, so the film must stay while any screening still references it, which costs a full scan of theaters and screenings that only runs on deletion.
tradeoff: 搜索结果正确 vs 每次删除付一次全量扫描
whenOtherWins: 若给每部电影维护引用计数，删除就能 O(1) 判断，代价是每次增删都要改计数。
optionExplanations: 扫描各影院场次，一发现还有引用就提前返回，保住搜索结果。
另一家影院的两场会立刻从搜索里消失，用户订不到在映电影。
按需重建要重新遍历全系统，等于把成本挪到每次搜索未命中。
永不清理会让下架电影一直出现在搜索里，点进去无场可订。
optionExplanations_en: It scans each theater's screenings and returns early on the first reference it finds, preserving correct search results.
The other theater's two screenings would vanish from search, so users cannot book a film that is still playing.
Rebuilding on demand re-walks the whole system, which just moves the cost onto every search miss.
Never cleaning up leaves withdrawn films in search results with nothing bookable behind them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录还有多少对象引用它，计数归零才真正回收，用于安全删除共享数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reference count tracks how many objects still point at a shared item, and only when it drops to zero is the item safe to remove.

scenario: 一家影院要永久关闭，它名下有 40 个未来场次，其中 6 场还有已付款的 active reservation。
scenario_en: A theater is closing permanently; it has 40 future screenings, six of which still hold paid active reservations.
q: 系统该怎么处理这次删除？
q_en: How should the system handle this deletion?
options: 拒绝删除，要求先取消并通知这 6 场的持票人
直接删影院，让这 6 份预订的 showtime 引用悬空
删影院但保留这 6 个场次在 showtimesById 里可订
自动为持票人改签到同城其它影院的同片场次
options_en: Reject the deletion until those six screenings are cancelled and ticket holders notified.
Delete the theater and let those six reservations point at nothing.
Delete the theater but keep the six screenings bookable in showtimesById.
Automatically rebook ticket holders into the same film at another theater in the city.
why: 删影院要级联清掉每个场次的 showtimesById 条目、theater 列表和不再上映的电影；任何 active reservation 都会变成指向空的确认号，所以先拒绝、清票再删。
why_en: Deleting a theater cascades through every screening's index entry and any film no longer showing, and any active reservation would be left pointing nowhere, so you reject first and clear the tickets before removing.
tradeoff: 拒绝删除的运维麻烦 vs 悬挂预订造成的数据损坏
whenOtherWins: 影院只是停业而非关闭时，更省事的做法是停排新场次、让存量场次自然过期。
optionExplanations: 取消加多渠道通知先跑完，删除就退化成纯结构清理。
持票人凭确认号查询会拿到一个不存在的场次，票据变废纸。
场次没有影院却仍可订，用户拿到一张不知道去哪看的票。
改签不在本题范围内，座位号和时间也未必对得上。
optionExplanations_en: Once cancellation and multi-channel notification have run, the deletion degrades into pure structural cleanup.
A ticket holder looking up their confirmation id gets a screening that no longer exists, so the ticket is worthless.
A screening with no theater is still bookable, handing the user a ticket with nowhere to go watch it.
Rebooking is out of scope here, and neither the seat numbers nor the times are guaranteed to line up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 删掉一个对象时必须连带清理所有引用它的结构，否则留下无法访问的孤儿数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascading delete must also clear every structure referencing the removed object, otherwise orphaned unreachable data is left behind.

termDefinitions.meaning: 尚未被取消、仍然占着座位的预订，删除任何上游对象前都要先处理它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An active reservation is one that has not been cancelled and still owns seats, so it must be resolved before deleting anything upstream.

scenario: 取消一整场演出要通知所有持票人，渠道有邮件、短信和 App 推送，将来还可能加微信。
scenario_en: Cancelling a whole screening means notifying every ticket holder over email, SMS and push, with WeChat likely to be added later.
q: Showtime 该怎么触达这些渠道？
q_en: How should Showtime reach those channels?
options: 发一个取消事件，各监听者自行决定怎么通知
在 cancel 里依次调用邮件、短信、推送三个客户端
把渠道列表配在 Showtime 上，按配置循环调用
让每个渠道轮询 showtime 状态，发现取消就发通知
options_en: Emit one cancellation event and let each listener decide how to notify.
Call the email, SMS and push clients one after another inside cancel.
Configure the channel list on Showtime and loop over the configuration.
Have each channel poll showtime state and send once it sees a cancellation.
why: Observer 让 Showtime 只发事件、不认识任何具体渠道，加微信只是多注册一个监听者；代价是调用链散开后，通知失败不再由 cancel 直接可见。
why_en: The observer pattern lets Showtime emit an event without knowing any channel, so adding WeChat is just one more listener, at the cost that a failed notification is no longer visible to cancel.
tradeoff: Observer 解耦渠道 vs 通知失败难以在主流程感知
whenOtherWins: 只有一个固定渠道且必须同步确认送达时，直接调用更简单也更好查。
optionExplanations: 一个事件对多个监听者，加渠道不用改 Showtime 一行代码。
每加一个渠道就要改 cancel，业务类被通知细节污染。
配置化只是把 if 换成循环，Showtime 仍然认识渠道接口。
轮询要各渠道自己扫状态，延迟高且重复扫描全量场次。
optionExplanations_en: One event feeds many listeners, so adding a channel changes not a single line of Showtime.
Every new channel edits cancel, polluting a business class with delivery details.
Configuration only swaps an if-chain for a loop; Showtime still knows the channel interface.
Polling makes each channel scan state itself, which is high latency and rescans every screening repeatedly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事件源只广播事件，多个监听者各自订阅并处理，事件源不认识监听者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In the observer pattern the event source only broadcasts, and multiple listeners subscribe and react without the source knowing any of them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个事件被分发给多个下游接收方，各自独立处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one event is dispatched to several downstream receivers that each handle it independently.

scenario: 加入 hold 后座位只有 available、held、booked 三态，规则只有两条禁止：不能 hold 已 booked 的座位、不能 book 别人 held 的座位。
scenario_en: With holds added a seat has only three states, available, held and booked, and only two rules: you cannot hold a booked seat and cannot book someone else's held seat.
q: 要不要把状态建模成对象？
q_en: Should each state be modeled as its own object?
options: 不要，三态用字段加两个 if 判断就够
要，每个状态建成一个类才能保证转换合法
要，State 模式是并发安全的前提
不要，改用枚举加一张完整的转换矩阵表
options_en: No, a field plus two if-checks covers three states.
Yes, only a class per state can guarantee transitions are legal.
Yes, the state pattern is a prerequisite for thread safety.
No, use an enum plus a full transition matrix table.
why: 三个状态两条规则用字段就能表达，建一套状态类是 overkill；等状态涨到 reserved、in-payment、refunded 且转换成网状时，才值得把每个状态变成对象。
why_en: Three states and two rules fit in a plain field, so a class hierarchy is overkill until states like reserved, in-payment and refunded make the transitions genuinely tangled.
tradeoff: 字段判断的直白 vs 状态增多后 if 分支爆炸
whenOtherWins: 状态涨到五六个、转换规则互相交叉时，State 模式的显式合法转换才划算。
optionExplanations: 两条禁止规则写进 holdSeats 和 book 的入口检查即可。
三个类加一套转换接口，读一条规则要跳三个文件。
并发安全来自 synchronized 临界区，和状态怎么建模无关。
3×3 矩阵里绝大多数格子是空的，表反而比 if 更难读。
optionExplanations_en: The two prohibitions fit as entry checks inside holdSeats and book.
Three classes plus a transition interface means jumping through three files to read one rule.
Thread safety comes from the synchronized critical section and is unrelated to how states are modeled.
Most cells in a three-by-three matrix are empty, so the table reads worse than the if-checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个状态建成一个对象，各自声明它允许转到哪些状态，替代散落的 if 判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The state pattern turns each state into an object that declares which transitions it allows, replacing scattered if-checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为当前不存在的复杂度提前引入结构，代价是可读性和改动成本上升。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overkill is introducing structure for complexity that does not exist yet, paying in readability and change cost.

scenario: 漫威首映场想把 hold 超时压到 3 分钟防囤座，淡季工作日想放到 10 分钟让用户从容付款。
scenario_en: A Marvel premiere wants the hold timeout down to three minutes to stop seat hoarding, while an off-peak weekday wants ten minutes so users can pay calmly.
q: 超时值该怎么接进 Showtime？
q_en: How should the timeout be wired into Showtime?
options: 抽一个超时策略接口，按场次注入不同实现
在 holdSeats 里按场次热度写 if-else 分支
把超时值设成全局常量，取两者的中间值 5 分钟
让前端在调 holdSeats 时把超时值一起传进来
options_en: Extract a timeout policy interface and inject a different implementation per screening.
Write if-else branches inside holdSeats based on how hot the screening is.
Make the timeout a global constant at the five-minute midpoint.
Let the frontend pass the timeout in when it calls holdSeats.
why: Strategy 把「超时算多少」从 Showtime 里抽走，新策略只加一个实现类；代价是多一层间接，读代码时要先找到注入的是哪个实现。
why_en: The strategy pattern pulls the timeout decision out of Showtime so a new policy is one new class, at the cost of an indirection you must trace to know which policy is actually wired in.
tradeoff: 策略可插拔 vs 多一层间接、超时值不再一眼可见
whenOtherWins: 只有一套固定超时且短期不会变时，一个常量比接口更好读。
optionExplanations: Showtime 只调 strategy 算出超时，不认识具体的档期规则。
每加一种档期规则就要改 holdSeats，热点方法越改越脆。
折中值两头不讨好：首映仍被囤座，淡季用户仍来不及付款。
客户端可传超时等于把囤座能力交给不可信调用方。
optionExplanations_en: Showtime just asks the strategy for a timeout and knows nothing about specific scheduling rules.
Every new scheduling rule edits holdSeats, and that hot method gets more fragile with each change.
The midpoint satisfies neither side: premieres still get hoarded and off-peak users still run out of time.
Letting the client choose the timeout hands seat-hoarding power to an untrusted caller.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一段会变化的算法抽到接口后面，运行时注入不同实现来切换行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The strategy pattern hides a varying algorithm behind an interface so different implementations can be injected at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户或脚本反复占座却不付款，把热门场次的库存长期锁死。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Seat hoarding is when users or bots repeatedly hold seats without paying, locking up inventory for a hot screening.

scenario: 45 分钟 LLD 面试只剩 12 分钟写代码，Showtime.book/cancel、searchMovies 和各种 getter 都还没落笔。
scenario_en: Twelve minutes of coding time remain in a 45-minute LLD interview, and Showtime.book/cancel, searchMovies and all the getters are still unwritten.
q: 这 12 分钟该手写哪些方法？
q_en: Which methods deserve those twelve minutes of real code?
options: 手写 book 和 cancel，其余口述带过
从 getter 开始按类顺序往下写完
先手写 searchMovies，索引逻辑最能体现设计
四个类的骨架各写一点，保证覆盖面完整
options_en: Write book and cancel by hand and talk through the rest.
Start from the getters and work down class by class.
Write searchMovies first, since the index logic best shows the design.
Sketch a bit of all four classes so the coverage looks complete.
why: book 和 cancel 是并发、原子性和状态归属唯一同时出现的地方，也是评分点；代价是要主动声明哪些方法你只口述，否则面试官会当作漏掉。
why_en: Book and cancel are the only place concurrency, atomicity and where seat state lives all show up at once, so you write those and explicitly say which methods you are only narrating.
tradeoff: 深写高信号方法 vs 代码覆盖面看起来不完整
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确说想看索引设计，就把时间挪到 searchMovies 和构造函数。
optionExplanations: 临界区、all-or-nothing 校验、座位释放都集中在这两个方法。
getter 没有任何判断，写满一屏也拿不到评分信号。
搜索只是一次子串扫描，索引结构画在类图上就说清了。
四处半成品既跑不通也说不清，不如一处完整。
optionExplanations_en: The critical section, the all-or-nothing validation and seat release all live in exactly these two methods.
Getters contain no decision at all, so a screen full of them earns no signal.
Search is one substring scan, and the index structure is already clear from the class diagram.
Four half-finished stubs neither run nor explain anything, so one complete method is worth more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多座位预订先校验全部座位，任何一个不可用就整单失败、不留任何状态改动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: All-or-nothing validation checks every requested seat first, so if any one is taken the whole booking fails with no state change.

scenario: Junior 级 45 分钟面试，你写出了能跑通的 book/cancel 流程，面试官还没问到并发。
scenario_en: In a Junior-level 45-minute interview you've produced a working book/cancel flow and the interviewer hasn't raised concurrency yet.
q: 达到 Junior 级合格线需要做到哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which of these clear the Junior-level bar? (select all that apply)
options: 认出 BookingSystem 编排、Showtime 管座位状态、Reservation 记录预订这套划分
book 检查可用性再存储，cancel 移除预订并释放座位
拒绝非法座位 ID，正确处理座位已被占用的情况
不用提示，自己主动发现 check-then-act 竞态并给出加锁方案
options_en: Recognize the split: BookingSystem orchestrates, Showtime owns seat state, Reservation records the booking.
book checks availability before storing; cancel removes the reservation and frees the seats.
Reject invalid seat IDs and correctly handle an already-taken seat.
Spot the check-then-act race condition on your own, unprompted, and propose locking.
why: Junior 合格线是能建好实体划分、走通基础预订/取消路径并做基础校验；并发竞态不要求自己发现，给了提示能跟上就够。
why_en: Junior clears the bar by modeling entities correctly, running the basic book/cancel path, and doing basic validation — spotting the race condition unprompted is not required.
optionExplanations: 这三层职责划分是最基础的建模能力，Junior 必须能说清楚。
book/cancel 的基本读写逻辑走通是及格线，不涉及并发正确性。
基础校验属于最低限度的错误处理，Junior 应主动想到。
文章明确说这一步允许在提示下完成，主动独立发现属于 Mid/Senior 信号，不是 Junior 要求。
optionExplanations_en: This three-way split is the most basic modeling skill and Junior candidates must be able to explain it.
Getting the basic book/cancel read-write logic working is the bar, no concurrency correctness required yet.
Basic validation is the minimum error handling Junior candidates should think of on their own.
The article explicitly says a hint toward synchronization is fine at this level — finding it unprompted is a Mid/Senior signal, not a Junior requirement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检查条件、再据此写入的两步操作，中间没有原子性保护时会被并发线程插入导致错误结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A check-then-act race is a check-then-write pair with no atomicity between them, letting a concurrent thread slip in and cause a wrong outcome.

scenario: Mid-level 面试，你已经写出 Showtime 拥有座位状态和 synchronized book，索引也用上了。
scenario_en: In a Mid-level interview you've already written Showtime owning seat state with synchronized book, and you're using lookup indexes.
q: 哪些是 Mid-level 应该做到的？（多选）
q_en: Which of these should a Mid-level candidate get right? (select all that apply)
options: 清楚 reservations 列表就是座位可用性的唯一事实来源，不需要额外结构
有并发意识，用 synchronized 把检查和存储包进同一临界区
多座位预订失败时保证 all-or-nothing，不留部分成功状态
不需要提示，主动权衡 per-showtime 和 per-seat 锁并给出何时切换的判断
options_en: Understand that the reservations list alone is the single source of truth for seat availability, no extra structure needed.
Show concurrency awareness by wrapping check-and-store in one synchronized critical section.
Guarantee all-or-nothing on multi-seat bookings, no partial success left behind.
Without prompting, proactively weigh per-showtime versus per-seat locking and say when to switch.
why: Mid-level 要能自己想到并发问题并写出正确的锁方案，all-or-nothing 也要处理对；主动权衡两种锁粒度、给出切换判断是 Senior 才要求的深度。
why_en: Mid-level candidates should independently reach the concurrency fix and get all-or-nothing right; proactively weighing lock granularities is Senior-level depth.
optionExplanations: 这是 Showtime 状态设计的核心认知，Mid-level 应该能不靠提示说清楚。
文章明确要求 Mid-level 有并发意识并能写出 synchronized 方案，这已经超出 Junior 靠提示的水平。
all-or-nothing 校验属于正确性要求，Mid-level 必须处理对，不能留部分状态。
文章把这一层权衡放进 Senior 段落，Mid-level 不要求主动给出锁粒度切换的判断。
optionExplanations_en: This is the core Showtime state insight, and Mid-level candidates should articulate it unprompted.
The article explicitly expects Mid-level concurrency awareness and a working synchronized fix, beyond Junior's need for a hint.
All-or-nothing correctness is required at Mid-level with no partial state left over.
The article places this tradeoff in the Senior paragraph; Mid-level isn't expected to volunteer the lock-granularity switch judgment.

scenario: 运营连续两次调用 addShowtime，给同一部已在索引里的电影新增两个不同场次；每次都会执行 moviesById[movie.getId()] = movie。
scenario_en: Ops calls addShowtime twice in a row for two different showtimes of a movie that's already indexed; each call re-executes moviesById[movie.getId()] = movie.
q: 重复写入 moviesById 会有什么后果？
q_en: What happens from writing moviesById repeatedly for the same movie?
options: 没有副作用，同一 key 被同一个 movie 对象覆盖，索引状态不变
第二次调用会抛重复键异常，addShowtime 失败
moviesById 里会出现两条指向同一电影的记录，搜索结果重复
必须先查一次 moviesById 是否存在该 movie，存在就跳过赋值
options_en: No side effect: the same key gets overwritten by the same movie object, index state is unchanged.
The second call throws a duplicate-key exception and addShowtime fails.
moviesById ends up with two entries pointing at the same movie, duplicating search results.
You must check whether moviesById already has the movie before assigning.
why: 用 movie.getId() 做 key 覆盖写是幂等的：已存在的电影只是被同一个值重新赋值一次，不需要先查后写。
why_en: Keying by movie.getId() makes the map write idempotent — re-adding an already-indexed movie just overwrites the key with the same value, no check-then-write needed.
optionExplanations: Map 赋值本身就是覆盖语义，同一 key 写同一个值不会产生第二条记录。
Map 赋值不是插入语义，不存在重复键异常，这里没有抛错路径。
moviesById 以 movie id 为 key，同一 key 只能存一条，不会出现两条记录。
幂等写入正是省掉这一步检查的原因，直接赋值即可，这就是文章说的“idempotent map writes”。
optionExplanations_en: Map assignment is overwrite semantics, so writing the same value to the same key never creates a second entry.
Map assignment isn't insert semantics, so there is no duplicate-key exception path here.
moviesById is keyed by movie id, so one key holds exactly one entry, never two.
Idempotent writes are exactly why this check is skipped — assign unconditionally, matching the article's point about idempotent map writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作执行一次或多次，系统最终状态相同；这里指用 movie id 做 key 反复赋值不会改变结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent write means running the operation once or many times leaves the system in the same final state — here, repeatedly assigning by movie id changes nothing extra.

scenario: BookingSystem 构造时用一次 O(t × s) 遍历建好 moviesById 和 showtimesByMovieId，之后每次用户搜索都复用这份索引。
scenario_en: BookingSystem's constructor does one O(t × s) pass to build moviesById and showtimesByMovieId, and every later search reuses that index.
q: 补全 searchMovies 建索引前后的复杂度变化：
q_en: Fill in how indexing changes searchMovies' complexity.
text: 建索引前，每次 searchMovies 要遍历全部影院和场次，复杂度是 {{O(t × s)}}（t 为影院数，s 为每影院场次数）；建索引后，只需扫描 {{几百部}} 电影的标题索引，再取出匹配电影的未来场次，复杂度降到 {{O(匹配电影数 × 每部电影场次数)}}。
why: 索引把“每次搜索都扫全系统”的成本挪到构造时一次性付清；后续搜索只碰匹配到的电影和它们的场次，这个复杂度差是支撑高频搜索调用的关键。
why_en: Indexing pays the full O(t × s) scan once at construction, so every later search only touches matching movies and their showtimes — that's what makes frequent search calls cheap.

scenario: isValidSeatId 按 rows='A'..'Z'、num=0..20 校验：先取首字符做行号，再把剩余部分解析成整数做边界比较。
scenario_en: isValidSeatId checks rows 'A'..'Z' and num 0..20 by taking the first character as the row and parsing the rest as an integer bound check.
q: 提交座位 ID “A21” 会发生什么？
q_en: What happens when a client submits seat ID "A21"?
options: 校验失败，因为 21 超出 0-20 的座位号上限
校验通过，因为 A 是合法行号，行合法就足够
校验通过，系统会把它当成第 22 排处理
校验失败，因为 A 排已经在锁内被别的线程占用
options_en: Validation fails because 21 is outside the 0-20 seat-number range.
Validation passes because A is a valid row, and a valid row is enough.
Validation passes and the system treats it as row 22.
Validation fails because row A is already locked by another thread.
why: isValidSeatId 对行和号两段分别做边界检查，行合法不能替代号合法，二者必须都通过。
why_en: isValidSeatId bounds-checks both the row and the number; a valid row doesn't excuse an invalid number — both must pass.
optionExplanations: num 解析结果是 21，21 大于座位号上限 20，边界判断在这一步返回 false。
行和号两个条件用逻辑与连接，缺一不可，满足其中一项不能跳过另一项。
座位号解析只取原始整数参与区间比较，不存在把超范围号折算成新行号的逻辑。
这个判断属于纯格式校验，发生在进入 synchronized 块之前，跟锁竞争完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Parsing gives num=21, and 21 is greater than the 20 seat-number cap, so the bound check returns false here.
isValidSeatId ANDs the row and number checks together; passing one doesn't let you skip the other.
Seat-number parsing takes the raw integer for range comparison; there's no logic remapping an out-of-range number into a new row.
This check is pure format validation that runs before any synchronized block is entered — it has nothing to do with lock contention.

scenario: BookingSystem.book 先调用 showtime.book(reservation)，只有它成功返回后才执行 reservationsById[id] = reservation；设想把顺序倒过来，先写索引再调用 showtime.book。
scenario_en: BookingSystem.book calls showtime.book(reservation) first and only registers reservationsById[id] = reservation after it returns; imagine the order were flipped.
q: 把写索引挪到 showtime.book 之前会带来什么问题？
q_en: What breaks if the index write happens before showtime.book?
options: 座位不可用时 showtime.book 抛异常，索引却留下一条未入座的预订
没有影响，写索引和调用 showtime.book 互不依赖，顺序随意
会导致 showtime.book 内部的 synchronized 块提前释放锁
只会让 confirmationId 比正常情况生成得稍晚一点
options_en: When a seat is unavailable, showtime.book throws — but the index is left with an entry for a booking that never actually took a seat.
No effect, writing the index and calling showtime.book don't depend on each other, order is arbitrary.
It would cause the synchronized block inside showtime.book to release its lock early.
It would only make confirmationId get generated slightly later than normal.
why: showtime.book 才是真正决定座位能否入座的一步；先写索引会让它抛异常时留下一条从未被接受的假预订。
why_en: showtime.book is the step that actually decides if seats succeed; writing the index first leaves a phantom entry when it throws.
optionExplanations: book 失败会立刻抛异常返回，此时如果索引已提前写入，就会跟 Showtime 内部真实状态脱节。
索引记录只有建立在预订被真正接受之上才可信，先后顺序正是决定这份可信度的关键。
两把锁彼此独立：写索引不会持有 Showtime 内部那把锁，顺序调整不影响它的释放时机。
confirmationId 在构造 Reservation 对象时就已生成，跟索引写入的先后顺序没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: book throws immediately on failure; if the index was already written by then, it drifts away from Showtime's real internal state.
The index entry is only trustworthy once the booking is truly accepted — ordering is exactly what makes that trust hold.
The two locks are unrelated: the index write never holds Showtime's internal lock, so reordering doesn't touch when it releases.
confirmationId is generated when the Reservation object is constructed, independent of when the index write happens.

scenario: cancelReservation 先调用 showtime.cancel(reservation) 让座位真正释放，再执行 reservationsById.remove(confirmationId)；设想把顺序倒过来，先删索引。
scenario_en: cancelReservation calls showtime.cancel(reservation) first to actually free the seats, then removes reservationsById[confirmationId]; imagine that order reversed.
q: 先删索引、再调用 showtime.cancel 会有什么风险？
q_en: What's the risk of removing the index entry before calling showtime.cancel?
options: 此时若进程崩溃，座位仍占用着，但用户已找不到 confirmationId 重试取消
没有风险，索引删除和座位释放两件事本来就互不依赖
会导致 Showtime.reservations 列表里同一条预订被重复删除两次
只会让取消操作的响应时间变慢，不影响最终结果
options_en: If the process crashes right then, the seats stay booked, but the user can no longer find that confirmationId to retry cancelling.
No risk, index removal and seat release are independent operations that don't rely on each other.
It would cause the same entry in Showtime.reservations to be removed twice.
It would only slow down the cancel response, not change the outcome.
why: showtime.cancel 才是真正释放座位的一步；先删索引等于提前切断用户找回这条预订的入口。
why_en: showtime.cancel is what actually frees the seats; removing the index first cuts off the user's only path back to this reservation.
optionExplanations: 一旦此时进程中断，座位仍留在 Showtime 里，但用户手上已经没有能再次触发释放的凭证。
索引原本是路由到释放座位那一步的入口，先删掉它会让后续操作失去依据，两者存在先后依赖。
reservations 的删除只会在释放座位那一步内部执行一次，删索引的先后顺序不会让它多跑一遍。
这不只是变慢，而是用户彻底失去重新触发释放座位的路径，属于正确性问题而不是性能问题。
optionExplanations_en: If the process stops right there, the seats stay inside Showtime, but the user no longer holds a credential that can trigger release again.
The index is the entry point that routes to the seat-release step; deleting it first strips away what that later step depends on.
The reservation removal runs exactly once inside the seat-release step regardless of when the index gets deleted — no double removal.
This isn't about latency — it's the user permanently losing the path to free the seats, a correctness gap, not a performance one.

scenario: Theater.getShowtimesForMovie 对自己的 showtimes 列表做线性扫描；BookingSystem.searchMovies 则依赖构造时建好的 showtimesByMovieId 全局索引。
scenario_en: Theater.getShowtimesForMovie does a linear scan over its own showtimes list, while BookingSystem.searchMovies relies on the global showtimesByMovieId index built at construction.
q: 为什么 Theater 级别的过滤不需要像 BookingSystem 一样建索引？
q_en: Why doesn't Theater-level filtering need an index the way BookingSystem does?
options: 一家影院的场次规模小，线性扫描已经够快，建索引的收益覆盖不了维护成本
Theater 类不允许出现任何循环语句，只能用索引结构
因为 Theater 不持有 showtimes 列表，没有数据可扫
因为这个过滤方法只在系统启动时被调用一次
options_en: A single theater's showtime count is small, so a linear scan is already fast enough that indexing wouldn't pay for its upkeep cost.
The Theater class isn't allowed to contain loops, only index structures.
Theater doesn't hold a showtimes list, so there's nothing to scan.
This filter method is only ever called once at system startup.
why: 扫描规模决定要不要建索引：BookingSystem 面向全系统场次选择建索引，Theater 只需扫自己那几十场，线性扫描比额外维护一份索引更划算。
why_en: Scan size decides whether indexing pays off: BookingSystem indexes because it spans every showtime in the system, while Theater only scans its own handful, where a linear scan beats maintaining another index.
tradeoff: 全系统跨影院建索引 vs 单个影院内小规模线性扫描
whenOtherWins: 如果某家影院自己的场次量涨到成千上万（比如巨型多厅影城长期排片），线性扫描也会变慢，届时才值得给 Theater 单独建一份按电影分组的索引。
optionExplanations: 同样是“建索引 vs 扫描”的取舍，规模不同结论就不同：全系统场次值得建索引，单影院几十场用不上。
建模语言本身没有禁止循环的规则，这个过滤方法本来就是一个普通 for 循环实现。
Theater 的核心状态正是它自己持有的 showtimes 列表，过滤方法正是在遍历这份数据。
浏览该影院节目单会在任何时刻触发这次过滤，不是只跑一次的启动逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: It's the same index-vs-scan tradeoff at a different scale — system-wide showtimes justify an index, a few dozen per theater don't.
There's no such language restriction; this filter is implemented as a plain for-loop.
Theater's core state is exactly its own showtimes list, and the filter method iterates over that data.
Browsing that theater's lineup can trigger this filter at any time, not just once at startup.

scenario: 一家影院即将永久关闭，运营想让它优雅下线而不是立刻从系统里删除。
scenario_en: A theater is permanently closing, and ops wants it to wind down gracefully instead of being deleted from the system immediately.
q: 文章建议的软下线做法是什么？
q_en: What's the article's suggested soft-decommission approach?
options: 停止给这家影院新增 showtime，让现有场次自然放映完并失效
立刻调用删除影院的级联接口，强制清空所有场次和预订
把这家影院的所有 showtime 转移到同城另一家影院名下
把 Theater 对象标记为 inactive 字段，其余逻辑保持不变
options_en: Stop adding new showtimes for that theater and let the existing ones play out and lapse naturally.
Immediately call the cascading theater-delete path, forcibly clearing every showtime and reservation.
Transfer all of that theater's showtimes to another theater in the same city.
Mark the Theater object with an inactive field and leave the rest of the logic unchanged.
why: 生产环境更常见的做法是不再排新场次，让已有场次自然放映完毕，回避了强制删除时要处理 active reservation 级联的复杂路径。
why_en: In production it's more common to simply stop scheduling new showtimes and let existing ones run their course, sidestepping the cascade-delete complexity around active reservations.
tradeoff: 停止新增让其自然落幕 vs 立即级联删除并强制清票
whenOtherWins: 如果影院要马上腾出场地（比如改造工程逼近截止日期），才值得走强制级联删除、拒绝并清理 active reservation 的重路径。
optionExplanations: 文章明确写道：如果影院要关闭，就停止新增场次，让已有场次放映完，这是比强制级联删除更简单的路径。
级联删除是明确保留给必须立刻处理场景的重路径，文章建议关闭场景优先走这种自然收尾而不是这条路。
文章没有描述任何转移 showtime 归属的机制，这属于凭空引入的新功能。
文章描述的软下线是行为上不再新增场次，而不是给 Theater 加一个新状态字段，这是多出来的机制，不是原文方案。
optionExplanations_en: The article states this directly: if a theater is closing, stop adding new showtimes and let the existing ones run out.
Cascading delete is the heavy path reserved for immediate removal; the article prefers this natural wind-down for a closing theater.
The article never describes any mechanism to move a showtime from one theater to another — that's an invented feature.
The soft-decommission the article describes is behavioral (stop scheduling), not a new inactive flag on Theater — that flag is an addition not in the source.

scenario: 用户在 hold 还剩 2 秒时提交支付，confirmHold 收到请求时 currentTime() 刚好已经超过 hold.expiresAt。
scenario_en: A user submits payment with 2 seconds left on their hold, and by the time confirmHold runs, currentTime() has just ticked past hold.expiresAt.
q: confirmHold 此时应该怎么处理？
q_en: What should confirmHold do in this case?
options: 拒绝确认并抛 HoldExpiredException，用户必须重新走一遍选座流程
忽略几秒钟的超时误差，照常把 hold 转成 reservation
把座位标记成一个新的、时限更长的 hold，让用户重新支付
静默把这次请求排到下一次 cleanupExpiredHolds 扫描后再处理
options_en: Reject the confirmation with HoldExpiredException, and the user has to restart seat selection.
Ignore the few seconds of drift and convert the hold to a reservation as usual.
Mark the seats with a new, longer-timeout hold so the user can pay again.
Silently queue the request until after the next cleanupExpiredHolds sweep.
why: confirmHold 按 currentTime() > hold.expiresAt 做严格判断，过期就直接拒绝并清掉这个 hold；文章承认这个紧凑竞态可能发生，但没有为它设计宽限期。
why_en: confirmHold makes a strict currentTime() > hold.expiresAt check and rejects immediately if expired; the article acknowledges this tight race can happen but doesn't design a grace period for it.
optionExplanations: 原文明说：如果 hold 在支付提交和确认之间过期，就拒绝并让用户重新开始，这是唯一被描述的行为。
confirmHold 的判断是严格的时间戳比较，没有任何“容忍几秒”的逻辑分支。
confirmHold 只写了拒绝或转正两条路径，没有描述任何自动续期的第三选项。
cleanupExpiredHolds 是独立跑的后台清理任务，不参与也不排队处理任何用户请求。
optionExplanations_en: The article's exact words: if the hold expires between payment submission and confirmation, reject it and the user starts over — the only described behavior.
confirmHold's check is a strict timestamp comparison with no seconds-of-tolerance branch.
confirmHold only has reject-or-convert as outcomes; there's no described auto-renewal third path.
cleanupExpiredHolds runs as an independent background sweep — it never defers or queues a user request.

scenario: 用户选座后拿到 5 分钟 hold，随即关闭浏览器弃单；没有任何 confirmHold 或 cancel 调用发生。
scenario_en: A user gets a 5-minute hold after picking seats, then closes the browser and abandons checkout — no confirmHold or cancel call ever happens.
q: 这些座位在系统里的状态会怎么演变？
q_en: How does the state of those seats evolve inside the system?
options: 过期未清扫前，座位仍暂时不可订
holds map 会到点自动清除该条目
座位立刻恢复可订，不受影响
座位永久锁死，需人工介入才能释放
options_en: Before the sweep runs, the seats remain temporarily unbookable.
The holds map automatically clears the entry the instant it expires.
The seats immediately become bookable again, unaffected.
The seats are locked forever and need manual ops intervention.
why: hold 过期只是一个时间判断，不会自己从 holds map 里消失；必须靠后台 cleanupExpiredHolds 定期扫描删除，代价是过期到被清扫之间座位对其他用户仍显示不可订。
why_en: An expired hold doesn't remove itself from the holds map — it takes the background cleanupExpiredHolds sweep to delete it, and the cost is a window where the seats still look unavailable to everyone else.
optionExplanations: 过期 hold 不会自动清理，要等下一次后台扫描任务把它从 map 里移除，座位才重新可订。
没有任何定时器或事件在到点那一刻主动触发删除，holds map 只是一个被动读写的数据结构。
isAvailable 会遍历 holds 并检查 expiresAt，还没被清扫的过期 hold 依然会让座位判定为不可用。
后台常规回收任务正是为了避免永久锁死而存在的机制，完全不需要人工介入。
optionExplanations_en: An expired hold doesn't clean itself up — the next background sweep has to remove it before the seats are bookable again.
No timer or event fires at expiresAt to trigger deletion; the holds map is a purely passive read/write structure.
isAvailable iterates holds and checks expiresAt, so an expired-but-unswept hold still marks the seat unavailable.
The routine background reclamation task exists precisely to avoid permanent lock-up, so no manual intervention is ever needed.

scenario: getShowtimesAtTheater 直接接受一个 Theater 对象作为参数，而不是 theaterId 字符串；文章解释这是因为整个系统跑在单进程内存里。
scenario_en: getShowtimesAtTheater takes a Theater object directly instead of a theaterId string; the article explains this is because the whole system runs in one process's memory.
q: 如果这套设计被拆成跨服务的网络化系统，这个参数选择要怎么变？
q_en: If this design were split into a networked, cross-service system, how would this parameter choice need to change?
options: 改传 theaterId，接收方按 ID 查询自己的数据副本
不需要变，对象引用可以直接通过网络传递给另一个服务
改传 Theater 对象的完整深拷贝，附带它全部的 showtimes 列表
把 Theater 类整体序列化成字符串塞进 URL 路径
options_en: Switch to passing theaterId, and have the receiver look it up against its own local data.
No change needed — object references can be sent over the network to another service directly.
Pass a full deep copy of the Theater object, including all of its showtimes.
Serialize the entire Theater class into a string and put it in the URL path.
why: 传对象引用之所以“更干净”是因为调用方和被调用方共享同一份内存；一旦跨进程，引用失去意义，只能传 ID 再由对方查自己的数据源。
why_en: Passing the object directly is cleaner only because caller and callee share the same memory; across a process boundary the reference is meaningless, so you pass an ID and let the other side look it up locally.
tradeoff: 进程内直传对象引用 vs 跨进程改传 ID 再查找
whenOtherWins: 只要调用方和被调用方仍在同一进程堆内存里，直传对象依然是更干净的选择，不必提前为分布式改造付索引化的代价。
optionExplanations: 这正是文章暗示的另一面：in-memory 系统才配直接传对象，网络化系统天然只能传标识符再查找。
对象引用是进程内内存地址的抽象，序列化后就失去身份含义，接收方也没有这块内存可用。
深拷贝整份 showtimes 会把一个简单的路由参数变成一次沉重的数据搬运，且拷贝立刻就会过时。
序列化整个类不是这套设计要解决的问题，Theater 还含有其它引用字段，直接塞进 URL 并不现实。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the flip side the article implies: only an in-memory system affords passing objects directly; a networked one is naturally reduced to IDs plus lookups.
An object reference is an in-process memory address abstraction; once serialized it loses that identity and the receiver has no such memory to resolve it against.
Deep-copying the whole showtimes list turns a simple routing parameter into a heavy data transfer that's stale the moment it's copied.
Serializing the whole class isn't the problem this design solves, and Theater holds other reference fields that don't fit cleanly into a URL.

scenario: 面试官追问：既然 per-showtime 锁牺牲了一些并行度，为什么不直接上 per-seat 锁把吞吐做到最大？
scenario_en: The interviewer presses: since per-showtime locking sacrifices some parallelism, why not just go straight to per-seat locking for maximum throughput?
q: 文章给出的一个回应角度是什么？
q_en: What's one angle the article offers in response?
options: 生产环境里真正的瓶颈是数据库写入，不是这把内存锁，优化锁粒度前先看瓶颈在哪
per-seat 锁在任何场景下都比 per-showtime 更简单，应该直接上
只要不用锁，数据库自然就不会成为瓶颈
锁粒度和数据库瓶颈无关，两者是两条完全独立的技术选型
options_en: The real bottleneck in production is database writes, not this in-memory lock — check where the bottleneck actually is before optimizing lock granularity.
Per-seat locking is simpler than per-showtime in every scenario, so it should be the default.
As long as you avoid locks, the database naturally stops being a bottleneck.
Lock granularity and database bottlenecks are two completely unrelated technology choices.
why: 文章提醒：真上生产后数据库才是限速环节，这把内存锁本身不是瓶颈；先确认瓶颈位置，再决定要不要为了吞吐上更复杂的 per-seat 锁。
why_en: The article notes that in production the database is the real bottleneck, not this in-memory lock — so confirm where the bottleneck actually is before reaching for the more complex per-seat lock.
tradeoff: 继续优化不是瓶颈的内存锁 vs 先确认数据库才是真正限速点
whenOtherWins: 一旦压测证明这把内存锁本身就是限速点（比如极高并发的单一热门场次），per-seat 锁的复杂度才真正值得付。
optionExplanations: 这是文章原话的立场：in-memory 锁不是生产瓶颈，数据库才是，为一个不是瓶颈的地方加复杂度收益有限。
文章反复强调 per-seat 锁复杂度更高（死锁风险、双份状态），从不认为它默认更简单。
去掉内存锁不会改变数据库本身的写入能力，数据库瓶颈和有没有用内存锁是两回事。
两者的关系正是这张卡的重点：锁粒度优化的收益要放进“数据库才是真瓶颈”这个背景下评估，不是互不相关。
optionExplanations_en: This mirrors the article's stance: the in-memory lock isn't production's bottleneck, the database is, so adding complexity where it isn't the bottleneck buys little.
The article repeatedly stresses per-seat locking is more complex (deadlock risk, dual state), never that it's simpler by default.
Removing the in-memory lock doesn't change the database's own write capacity — the two are separate concerns.
Their relationship is exactly the point of this card: lock-granularity gains should be judged against the database being the real bottleneck, not treated as unrelated.

scenario: Class Design 阶段讨论 BookingSystem 时，面试官问 book 和 cancel 具体怎么高效定位到 showtime 和 reservation。
scenario_en: During the Class Design discussion of BookingSystem, the interviewer asks exactly how book and cancel will efficiently locate the right showtime and reservation.
q: 这个阶段的合理回应是什么？
q_en: What's the right response at this stage of the interview?
options: 说明这是实现细节，方法签名先定好，效率问题留到 Implementation 阶段
当场停下来，把 showtimesById 等三个索引的完整构造函数全部写出来
回避这个问题，直接跳到 Showtime 的并发设计上
承认自己不知道，请面试官直接给出完整索引方案
options_en: Name it as an implementation detail, lock down the method signature now, and save the efficiency question for the Implementation phase.
Stop right there and write out the full constructor for all three indexes.
Dodge the question and jump straight to Showtime's concurrency design.
Admit you don't know and ask the interviewer to just hand you the full indexing scheme.
why: 文章把这个问题标成“an implementation detail we'll tackle later”，类设计阶段只需定好接口和职责，索引这类效率优化留到下一阶段集中处理。
why_en: The article explicitly tags this as an implementation detail to tackle later — at the class-design stage you only need the interface right, leaving efficiency optimizations like indexes for the next phase.
tradeoff: 当场展开索引实现 vs 先标注为后续实现细节、稳住类设计节奏
optionExplanations: 这正是文章展示的沟通技巧：先说清楚这是后面才解决的实现细节，避免类设计阶段被效率问题拖慢。
提前把索引构造全部写出来会打乱面试节奏，文章把这部分放进了后面的 Implementation 小节。
回避问题和明确标注“稍后处理”不是一回事，前者会让面试官觉得没听到问题。
这是候选人自己该做的设计判断，不是面试官该替你回答的部分。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the communication move the article demonstrates: flag it as a later implementation detail so the class-design stage isn't derailed by efficiency questions.
Writing out the full index construction early derails the interview's pace; the article places this in the later Implementation section.
Dodging the question and explicitly deferring it are different — the former reads as not having heard the question.
This is a design judgment the candidate is expected to make, not something to offload onto the interviewer.

scenario: 前端每次打开某个 showtime 的座位选择页都会调用一次 getAvailableSeats，返回当前可订座位列表。
scenario_en: Every time the frontend opens a showtime's seat-picker page it calls getAvailableSeats once to get the current bookable seats.
q: 补全 getAvailableSeats 的复杂度分解：
q_en: Fill in the complexity breakdown of getAvailableSeats.
text: getAvailableSeats 先把已订座位收进一个 set，成本是 {{O(已订座位数)}}；再扫一遍固定布局取补集，成本是固定的 {{O(546)}}；前端每次打开座位图只调 {{一次}}，所以这个总成本可以忽略。
why: 已订座位集合大小随预订数增长但上限被 546 卡住，布局扫描是常数 546；两段成本相加，且只在用户打开页面这个低频事件上发生，所以不必为它额外优化。
why_en: The booked-seat set grows with bookings but is capped at 546 seats total; the layout scan is a flat 546; both costs only run on the low-frequency page-open event, so no extra optimization is warranted.

scenario: removeShowtime 在 showtime.getReservations() 非空时直接抛 ShowtimeHasActiveReservationsException，拒绝删除；这个 showtime 之后收到一个 cancelReservation 调用。
scenario_en: removeShowtime throws ShowtimeHasActiveReservationsException and refuses to delete whenever showtime.getReservations() isn't empty; later, that showtime receives a cancelReservation call.
q: cancelReservation 需要额外处理“showtime 已被删除”这种情况吗？
q_en: Does cancelReservation need to separately handle the case where its showtime has already been removed?
options: 不需要，只要 reservation 还在索引里，它引用的 showtime 就一定没被删除
需要，必须先检查 showtimesById 里是否还有这个 showtime
需要，因为 removeShowtime 可以在有 active reservation 时强制删除
不需要，因为 cancelReservation 根本不会用到 Reservation 的 showtime 引用
options_en: No — as long as the reservation is still in the index, the showtime it references is guaranteed not to have been removed.
Yes — it must first check whether showtimesById still contains that showtime.
Yes — because removeShowtime can force-delete even with active reservations.
No — because cancelReservation never uses the Reservation's showtime reference at all.
why: 有 active reservation 的 showtime 永远删不掉，是 removeShowtime 守卫保证的不变量；只要预订还在索引里，back-reference 就一定有效。
why_en: removeShowtime's guard maintains an invariant that a showtime with active reservations can never be deleted, so a reservation still in the index guarantees a live back-reference.
optionExplanations: 两处代码合起来保证这条不变量：一旦发现有票就直接拒绝删除，取消流程因此不会遇到悬空引用。
多一次查表只是在重复这条不变量已经替你保证的事，属于不必要的防御性代码。
这个守卫方法一发现 reservations 非空就抛异常返回，代码里没有强制删除这条分支。
cancelReservation 恰恰靠 reservation.getShowtime() 这个反向引用找到该路由到哪个 Showtime，这是它的核心步骤。
optionExplanations_en: The two pieces of code jointly guarantee this invariant: deletion is refused as soon as tickets are found, so the cancel flow never meets a dangling reference.
An extra lookup would just re-check something this invariant already guarantees — unnecessary defensive code.
This guard method throws and returns the moment reservations is non-empty; there is no force-delete branch in the code.
cancelReservation relies exactly on reservation.getShowtime() to find which Showtime to route to — that's its core step.
